label: Appearance
params: bodies?: [names]; faces?: [[x,y,z] on faces] (body?: which body, default the nearest); components?: [names or ids, or occurrence names]; appearance?: library name or stable starter.* ID (appearance.library) | color: "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0–255), opacity? (0–1, default 1); name?: inert copied look label (requires color, mutually exclusive with appearance); pbr?: {metallic:0..1, roughness:0.045..1, dielectric_ior:1..3} (requires color/appearance and opacity 1); a starter ID or registered starter name resolves its recipe before color overrides; omitted pbr retains that response and pbr: null explicitly clears it. Unavailable glass recipes refuse through either selector. Other custom labels with an explicit color retain legacy scalar behavior. Neither appearance nor color (or color: null): clear, so the face follows its body, the body its component, the component its material

label: Appearance Chain
params: target: {body: name} | {body: name, face: zero-based model.faces index} | {component: name or id}; a placed copy's name (`KB (K:2)`, `K:2`) means the body or component it shows. Returns steps [{step: face|body|component|material, look: {name,color,opacity,pbr?} or null}] in precedence order and active (step or null). Component material is the common default look of its directly owned bodies, null if mixed/empty. Imported paint is a display fallback outside the four steps. Read-only; no dialogs

label: Copy Look
params: target: appearance.chain target. Copies its resolved look to a transient session clipboard. No document change or dialogs.

label: Favorite Look
params: look: appearance.assign look keys (appearance, or color/name/opacity/pbr); favorite: true to mark, false to unmark → the validated look and the preference; UI library preference only, no document change or dialogs.

label: Appearance Library
params: → 20 legacy scalar appearances, six opaque PBR finishes and 40 starter recipes with IDs, categories, provenance, requirements and availability; six starter glass recipes are unavailable

label: List Appearances
params: body?: name (or a placed copy's, `KB (K:2)`: the body it shows) → assigned appearances; with body, its resolved look and its faces' (face index, look)

label: Paint Appearance
params: appearance or color/name/opacity/pbr: appearance.assign look parameters; validates and returns look for ui.start paint. done?: true ends the UI tool. Programmatic calls never open UI.

label: Paste Look
params: bodies/faces/components: appearance.assign targets, and no look keys: the look is the one appearance.copy put in the clipboard. Applies it atomically in one undo step; no dialogs.

label: Pick Up Appearance
params: target?: appearance.chain target; returns its resolved look, or requests the UI sampling tool when omitted. Programmatic calls never open UI.

label: Replace Appearance
params: from: library name | saved look {name,color,opacity,pbr?} (copy appearance.list in_design); to: library name | assignment look {appearance? | color, name?, opacity?, pbr?} (appearance.assign rules; no clear). Matches the full look including name and PBR. scope?: {bodies?: [names], components?: [names or ids]} (a placed copy's name means the body or component it shows), at most 10000 targets; body scope includes face overrides, component scope selects only the component override. Omitted scope means all overrides, including hidden/suppressed ones; physical defaults are unchanged. Duplicate targets count once. Returns count of rewritten overrides; zero adds no history. One undo step, atomic; no dialogs. Designs above 100000 overrides refuse

label: Bill of Materials
params: component?: id or name (default the design); levels?: flat (default: every part at any depth, counted through its subassemblies) | top (the component's direct children, subassemblies as one row each) | all (as top, each subassembly's own rows listed after it, to any depth: items 1.1, 1.1.1, as in the CSV); show_purchased_contents?: true (in all, a purchased part's contents listed under it too); show_suppressed_parts?: true (a part a configuration switches off, with no bodies and a suppressed feature of its own, listed as placed; by default it counts nowhere); group_by?: ["part_number"] (default; components without a part number get a row per definition) | ["definition"]; group_children?: true (a component with a part number is one row, the parts placed inside it listed under it as children: [{item, part_number, description, revision, each, count, definition, material, mass_g?}], not as rows of their own); mass?: true (measures each part: mass_g, what one of the row's parts weighs in grams with what is placed inside it, except what the list shows as rows of their own beside it (in parts only a part's contents are rows of their own, but not a folded part's or a purchased one's, and of an inseparable one's only its purchased parts are), so the rows add up to the assembly; a reference placement adds nothing; null when nothing in it has a body, a body can't be measured or the row's definitions differ); path?: write a .csv (columns item, part_number, description, revision, count, definition, material, quantity, finish) or .json file (children as items 1.1, 1.2…); format?: csv|json (default from the path). Each placement counts as its occurrence's bom_type, else its component's: phantom has no row (what it holds counts here; its own bodies, if it has any, are a row of their own), reference counts nowhere, purchased and inseparable are one row (in flat, an inseparable one's purchased parts are listed too, under it with group_children and a part number); placements of one component that count as different types are different rows → rows: [{item, part_number, description, revision, bom_type, count, definition, finish (the part's finish property, else a free property named finish), material (the physical materials of the definitions' own bodies, "; " between them; a row that weighs what is placed inside it shows the one material all of that shares, else ""), mass_g?, quantity? (when its definitions have a bom_quantity: what its placements add up to, a number with quantity_unit pieces or mm, a placement without one counting 1 piece; null with quantity_unknown mixed (pieces and a length) or invalid (a quantity that no longer evaluates)), components, properties, children?, static? (["material"]: a value typed in for the component, shown in place of the worked-out one)}] sorted by part number, total_occurrences (children included), total_mass_g (with mass: what the assembly weighs, measured from the design rather than added up from rows; null when unknown), numbered (the view's item numbers are saved: assembly.bom.renumber). In a numbered view each level is listed by item number and a row says provisional (its number not saved yet: a row added since shows the next number at its level, saved by the next change), locked and duplicate when true

label: Change Item Number
params: component?, levels?, group_by?, group_children?, show_purchased_contents?, show_suppressed_parts?: the view, as assembly.bom takes them; row: the row's item as the view shows it now ("3", or "1.2" under row 1); item?: 1 to 999999 (a number another row has is allowed: both are marked duplicate); locked?: true|false (a renumber keeps a locked number). A view not numbered yet is numbered first, every row keeping the number it shows. One undo step → the view as assembly.bom gives it, with duplicates: [item numbers used twice at the row's level]

label: Renumber Items
params: component?, levels?, group_by?, group_children?, show_purchased_contents?, show_suppressed_parts?: the view, as assembly.bom takes them; start?: 1; step?: 1 (whole numbers, 1 to 999999); order?: list (default: by part number, as an unnumbered view lists) | item (in item-number order, closing the gaps). Numbers every row from start by step, each level on its own (in all levels, within its parent); locked rows keep their numbers and the others skip them; rows that are gone are forgotten. Saves the view's numbers, with these list options: after it, a row added takes the highest number at its level + 1 and a row removed leaves a gap until the next renumber. One undo step → the view as assembly.bom gives it

label: Constrain
params: type: mate|flush|distance|concentric|insert|parallel|perpendicular|angle|tangent|point_on_axis; a, b: references, as joint.create's origins (a face or a datum plane for a plane, a circle or an axis for an axis, a point; a round face given as a face is its axis where the rule needs one; b moves); offset?: the gap (mm or an expression; needed for distance); angle?: deg or an expression (needed for angle); flip?: turn b over; name? (default: the rule and a number, Mate1); quiet?. Kept as a joint of the kind the rule needs (mate and flush planar, distance planar or point on plane, concentric cylindrical, insert revolute, tangent line on plane, point on axis point on line), made where the parts are, so b moves no further than the rule needs → joint, name, dof, conflicts, fixed as joint.create

label: Edit Constraint
params: constraint: id|name (a joint made with assembly.constraint.create); type?: a rule as assembly.constraint.create takes it (the references it has must fit it; the gap carries over); offset?: the gap (mm or an expression); angle?: an angle rule's angle; flip?: true turns b over (from the new rule's way after a type change, else from how it faces now); name?; suppressed?; quiet?. Changed as joint.edit changes a joint: its values start again where its parts are → conflicts, errors, dof, fixed as joint.edit

label: Mass Properties
params: no parameters → occurrences: [{occurrence (0: the design's own bodies), name, component, path, group, fixed, frame {origin, x, y, z}, bodies: [{name, material, density_g_cm3, closed, volume_mm3, mass_kg}], open_bodies_skipped, mass}], groups: [{group, occurrences, fixed, frame_occurrence, frame, mass}] (occurrences an unsuppressed rigid joint ties together, and a nested occurrence no joint places with its parent; fixed: holds the design or a grounded occurrence), warnings. mass: {mass_kg, center_of_mass_mm (world), center_of_mass_local_mm, inertia_world_kg_mm2, inertia_local_kg_mm2 (about the centre of mass, in world and frame axes)} or null when massless. Read-only; pending moves count; each body at its material's density (the default material's when none is assigned)

label: Collision Shape
params: body: its name, or component: id or name for all its bodies; shape: auto|mesh|box|cylinder|sphere|none: what it looks like to a simulator (URDF export; box, cylinder and sphere are set in the body's bounding box)

label: Print Face
params: body: its name; point?: [x, y, z] on a flat face of it, in mm (omit to clear) → {body, face?}: marks the face a slicer export (file.send_to_slicer, file.save_mesh with slicer, file.open_in_easyprint), or an STL or 3MF export with lay_on_print_faces (file.export, file.export_stl, file.export_3mf, file.save_mesh), lays the body on: turned so the face points down at Z = 0, the centre of mass over the origin. One per body, replacing the last; flat faces of solid bodies only. A print face that is gone or no longer flat is reported in the export's warnings, and the body exported as it lies

label: Check Print Faces
params: bodies?: name | [names] (default every body) → {bodies: [{body, status: set | none | lost, face?, problem?}], all_set}: whether each body has a print face (body.print_face) that an export would lay it on; lost: one was marked but the face is gone or no longer flat (problem says why). all_set is true when at least one body was checked and every one is set. Read-only

label: Remove History
params: body: its name → feature, name: the base feature that now holds the body's B-rep; removed: [the features that went: those that built only this body, and the sketches only they used]; kept: [features that built this body and also build or change other bodies, so they stay]; remove?: the Remove feature added before the base when kept features still build the body; faces, edges, vertices, volume_before, volume_after: the body before and after; broken: [{feature, error}] (features that worked and now fail); notes?: [references to the body's faces that could not move to the base feature's]. One undo step; refused, with why, when nothing can be removed

label: Rename Body
params: body: its name, or bodies: several body names (each in turn gets the first of name, name (2), name (3)… that no other body has), name: the new name (features that use the bodies follow)

label: Repair Part
params: body: its name (a part the modelling kernel refuses, or an open part that should be a solid); gap?: expr (default 0.2 mm, at most 1 mm: free edges that pair up within it are sewn, each sewn edge carrying its own gap as its tolerance); patch_holes?: bool (default false: loops of free edges left are patched, in the plane of the faces around them where those are that plane, else tangent to them, and sewn in; otherwise the reply offers the patches); name? → the feature, and repair: what changed face by face (rebuilt and refused faces, sewn gaps, holes with their surface.patch), faces and largest edge tolerance before and after, closed, modelling, volume. Refused with why when nothing applies

label: Collapse All
params: path?: [occurrence ids] (that placement's branch); component?: id; omit both for the whole tree: every placement, folder and group at every level. The row it starts from (the design row for the whole tree) stays open, so its first level remains visible. Display only; not an undo step → open, open_by_default, closed_by_default

label: Expand All
params: path?: [occurrence ids] (that placement and its descendants); component?: id (that component's own folders); omit both for the whole tree, including folders that start closed (Origin, Named Views, Features). Display only: open/closed rows are not saved in the design and are not an undo step → open, open_by_default, closed_by_default

label: Search the Browser
params: text?: what the names hold, ignoring case (with * for any text or ? for any one character it must match the whole name: *:1 ends in :1; at most 256 characters); kinds?: [component|body|sketch|construction|joint] (default every kind; give text, kinds or both) → {found: [{kind, name, key, path, item?}], total, incomplete}: every placement of a component is its own match, path is the placement it is in, item is what select.set takes (a joint has none; its key is its id); at most 10000 listed, total counts them all

label: New Group
params: folder?: bodies|sketches|construction; component?: id (default 0); parent?: group id (the new group nests in it, taking its component and folder; at most 8 levels); name?; items?: [keys] (they leave other groups)

label: Isolate
params: clear?: bool. Without it, hides everything except the selection: the selected components' placements, or else the selected bodies and the bodies of the selected faces, edges and vertices, as browser.visibility with isolate:true; nothing selected is an error. clear:true ends the Isolate in effect instead, as browser.unisolate (the viewport status pill's close)

label: Move Browser Items
params: folder, component?, items: [keys (strings) and group ids (numbers)]; group?: id (into it; omit for the folder's top level); before?: key or group id (position in it; default the end). A group cannot go into itself or past 8 levels

label: Order Browser Items
params: folder: bodies|sketches|construction|components, component?, order: [keys (strings) and top-level group ids (numbers)] (display order; for `components`, the ids of the components placed in it)

label: Rename Group
params: group: id, name

label: Move to Component
params: Moves placements, features and bodies into a component. occurrences?: [ids or paths], features?: [ids or names], bodies?: [names], component?: where they go (default: the active one), component_path?: its placement → component, occurrences, features, bodies (what moved). One undo step, all or nothing: placements move first (taking what they hold), then features (taking the bodies they made), then the bodies still elsewhere (a body transfer, which leaves its features behind)

label: Show/Hide Planes
params: (no parameters) the origin planes (XY, XZ, YZ) and every construction plane: hidden when any of them shows, shown otherwise;          axes, points and sketches keep their state. Saved with the design and undone like browser.visibility

label: Show/Hide Reference Geometry
params: (no parameters) all reference geometry: the origin (point, axes, planes), every construction plane, axis and point, and every sketch;          hidden when any of it shows, shown otherwise (showing does not show a sketch a feature uses unless it was shown on its own).          Bodies and joints keep their state. Saved with the design and undone like browser.visibility

label: Ungroup
params: group: id (its items and child groups go up to the group that holds it, or the folder)

label: Exit Isolation
params: (no parameters) as browser.visibility with visible:true and unisolate:true: puts back what the isolates hid; with nothing isolated it is an error and shows nothing

label: Show/Hide
params: visible: bool; items?: [sketch id or name | body name | construction name | joint name | O|X|Y|Z|XY|XZ|YZ]; or joints?: [joint id or name] (their glyphs; they still constrain and move parts); or features?: [feature id or name] (the bodies they made; path?: [occurrence ids] for only that placement's); or folder?: bodies|sketches|construction|origin|joints|all (all of it; showing also shows its browser folders and groups, and `all` takes in the occurrence hides too); or tree_folders?: [browser folder or group key: c0/bodies, o:4/sketches, o:4/origin, c0/g7, c0/joints, c0/canvases, c0/point_clouds] (the folder or group itself: its items keep their own state; component origin items use o:4/origin/XY etc. in items); or paths?: [[occurrence ids]] (exact placements and descendants), isolate?: bool (with paths or items of bodies, and visible:true: everything else is hidden, other placements as placements); or unisolate?: bool (with visible:true and no target: put back what the isolates since the last unisolate hid, or show everything). Saved with the design and undone like any other change (the camera is not)

label: Calibrate Canvas
params: canvas: id or name; a, b: two points on the canvas plane [x,y]; distance: their true distance (mm): scales the image about a

label: Decal
params: path: a PNG, JPEG or SVG file; resolution?: pixels (an SVG's longest side, default 1024); face: [x,y,z] on a planar face (the image is centred there), or the picked face as sketch.create's plane takes it ({face, body, index, path?}); width?: mm; angle?: deg; opacity?: (default 1); frame?: true ties the image to a construction rectangle around it, as canvas.frame_sketch does; "auto" only in the sketch being edited, when the face is on its plane. A decal is part of the model's look: URDF export writes it as a textured visual of its component's link

label: Delete Canvas
params: canvas: id or name

label: Edit Canvas
params: canvas: id or name; center?, width?, angle?: deg, opacity?, flip?, visible?, name?, locked? (a locked canvas refuses center, width, angle, flip, Calibrate and Delete); anchor?: {sketch: id, bottom_left, bottom_right: point ids, top_left?: point id} | null (the sketch points the image's corners follow; without top_left the height follows the image; an anchored canvas refuses center, width, angle, Calibrate and Straighten)

label: Frame Sketch
params: canvas: id or name; name?: the new sketch's name. Draws a construction rectangle exactly around the image, in the sketch being edited (the image must lie on its plane) or else in a new sketch on the canvas's plane, and anchors the image's corners to it: dimension and constrain that rectangle to place and size the image → sketch, bottom_left, bottom_right, top_left (point ids)

label: Canvas
params: path: a PNG, JPEG or SVG file (an SVG is drawn into a PNG); resolution?: pixels (an SVG's longest side, default 1024, at most 4096); plane?: XY|XZ|YZ|{face: [x,y,z]}|… (default XY); center?: [x,y] on the plane, or at?: [x,y,z]; width?: mm (default 100); angle?: deg; opacity?: 0…1 (default 0.5); flip?; name?; frame?: true ties the image to a construction rectangle around it (in the sketch being edited, which it must lie on, else in a new sketch), as canvas.frame_sketch does; "auto" frames it in the sketch being edited only when it lies on its plane

label: Straighten Canvas
params: canvas: id or name; a, b: two points on the canvas plane [x,y] along a line of the image; angle?: deg, the direction that line should have (0 horizontal, the default; 90 vertical): turns the image about a, the shorter way

label: Canvas to Sketch
params: canvas?: id or name (default: the last canvas); name?: the new sketch's name. Traces the canvas image (dark drawing on a light background, or the reverse) into a new sketch on the canvas plane, lying exactly on the image: lines, splines and holes. at?: [x, y] a point on the canvas plane (mm); given, only the region joined to that point whose colour is within tolerance of the colour there is traced; tolerance?: colour difference 0-100 (default 20), with at

label: Activate Component
params: component: id or name (0 or "root" for the design); occurrence?, path?: exact placement used to author shared geometry

label: Break Link
params: component: id or name of a linked component — keeps its bodies as they are and forgets the source file, and the importer that read it

label: Capture Position
params: keeps pending occurrence moves and saves every moving joint's values → captured, joints

label: Find Identical Copies
params: component: id or name of a linked component → copies: [{component, name}], the components not linked whose own history builds the same bodies

label: Paste Bodies
params: bodies: [names, as the Browser shows them: a body seen in another placement of its component (`Cube (B:2)`) is copied from there]; component?: where the copies go (default: the active one); component_path?: its placement to place them by (default: its only one, else the active one; a component placed more than once gets them in every instance). Each copy stays where its body is in the world; the copies' names come back as `bodies`

label: New Component
params: name?, parent?: component id or name (default: the active one); parent_path?: exact parent placement; activate?: bool (default true); grounded?: bool (default: true for the design's first part, false otherwise); bom_quantity?: what one placement means in a bill of materials (component.metadata.set's); virtual?: true, a component with no geometry (grease, paint, a label): listed in bills of materials with its quantity, never active (default activate false; true is refused), and nothing can be put in it

label: Cycle Component Color
params: component: id or name; saves the next identification colour and turns Component Colors on; shared by every instance, separate from appearances

label: Delete Component
params: component: deletes it, its subcomponents, occurrences and features

label: Edit in Place
params: component: id or name of a linked component; path?: its placement (occurrence ids, default its first) → in the app window: open the design it links in a tab of its own with the assembly drawn around it (component.finish_edit goes back); fails when it is not linked, the assembly has no file yet, something is open or running in it, or the file is missing, on a network location not allowed yet or open in another SolidCraft; asked during the agent's turn it opens once the turn ends (queued: true); elsewhere it only checks

label: Extract to File
params: component: id or name of a component that is not linked; path: the .sc design to write → its history, subcomponents and their joints move to that design, and the component becomes linked to it (as component.insert_design makes it); returns path, file, feature, bodies, notices (what stays behind), warnings and copies (components that build the same bodies: see component.replace_with_link)

label: Finish Edit
params: no parameters → in the app window: go back from the linked design edited in place to its assembly, which reads it again; fails while the design has unsaved changes (run file.save first) or something is open in it; asked during the agent's turn it finishes once the turn ends (queued: true); elsewhere nothing changes

label: Create Components from Bodies
params: bodies: [names] → one new component per body, named after it

label: Hide Component History
params: component: id or name; keeps the component's features in the design but leaves them out of the History bar (#10393)

label: Insert Design
params: path: a .sc design, or a file an installed importer plugin reads (format?: its plugin.entry, default the importer that claims the extension; options?: its declared options) → a new component linked to it, holding its solid bodies as placed in that design, its canvases and decals where the design shows them, and a copy of its design properties; document?: the design itself, as its JSON, for a design open in the session that has no file yet: its bodies come in as they are and the link names no file (not with path); configuration?: a row name or id (null or omitted: the saved source state); name? (default: the design's name); parent?: component id or name (default: the active one); translate?: [x,y,z] in mm from the destination parent's origin (default [0,0,0], also with reuse); axis?: [x,y,z], angle?: radians or "30 deg", origin?: [x,y,z]; matrix?: [12 or 16 numbers] (row-major 3x4 or 4x4, its translation column numbers or length expressions) or to_matrix?: [12 or 16 numbers]; tolerance?: largest accepted |RᵀR − I| (default 1e-9, at most 1e-3); reuse?: bool (default false): insert a free occurrence, reusing an existing link to the same file and configuration when available

label: List Links
params: → linked components: component, name, path, importer? ({format, plugin?, version?}: `step` or the importer plugin that read the file; for a plugin also available (it is installed and on), installed_version (when it differs or it can't be used) and needs (which plugin and version the link needs and why it can't be used)), configuration (selected row id, omitted when following the saved source state), file (resolved), found (null when the file is on a network location not allowed, or names a device: it is not looked for), changed (whether the file is no longer what this design last read: Update Links reads it again; null when not found or the link is older than this record), then host (the network location); state (missing, unreadable, not_allowed: a network location not allowed or outside the folders this agent may use) and reason when the file can't be reached

label: List Components
params: compact?: bool (counts of bodies, features, sketches and construction planes instead of their names; occurrences leave out identity transforms; children as occurrence ids); bodies?: bool (with compact: body names, not their count)

label: Part Properties
params: component: id or name (0 or "root": the design's own properties) → component, name, part_number, description, revision, material (its static material or null), finish (or null), bom_type, bom_quantity (or null) and virtual (components only), metadata (as saved, other tools' keys too), properties: {name: text}

label: Change Part Properties
params: component: id or name (not the root: use document.metadata.set, which takes material and finish too); part_number?, description?, revision?: text (empty or null removes); finish?: text, the part's finish, free ("powder coat, RAL 9005, matt", "zinc plate, clear", "#4 brushed"; empty or null removes it); bom_type?: normal|phantom|reference|purchased|inseparable (empty or null: normal); material?: text, a static material: what its bill of materials rows say it is made of, in place of its bodies' materials (it doesn't change the mass; empty or null clears it); bom_quantity?: an expression, what one placement means in a bill of materials: a number of pieces ("4") or a length ("2.5 m", "2 * span + 50 mm"), evaluated with the design's parameters, above 0 (empty or null removes it: one piece); virtual?: true|false (a component with no geometry, such as grease or a label: it can't be the active component or hold bodies, sketches or components); values?: {key: value} (SolidCraft's keys, as document.metadata's properties lists them (material and finish too), bom_type, bom_quantity, virtual, or a reverse-DNS key holding an object); properties?: {name: text, …} (free properties; empty or null removes). All or nothing, one undo step → component, metadata, properties, changed: [keys]

label: Move Bodies to Component
params: bodies: [names], component; component_path?: its placement to place them by (default: its only one, else the active one; a component placed more than once gets them in every instance); from_path?: the placement of their component they move from (default: its only one, else its first, where its bodies have their own names)

label: Move Features to Component
params: features: [ids or names] (sketches too); component?: where they go (default: the active one) → moved, component, bodies. Ids, names and timeline order stay; the geometry stays where it is in the world; the bodies the features made move with them. Refused while the timeline is rolled back, for a component placed more than once, and for a move that would break a feature (nothing changes)

label: Move Sketches to Component
params: sketches: [ids or names] (a number is an id; a string is an exact name, then an id), component; the sketches keep their own coordinates (component.move_features keeps them where they are in the world), except that a sketch on an exactly attached face stays where it is on the face

label: Move Sketches to Their Parts
params: sketches?: [ids or names] (default: every sketch in the design) → moved, stayed, sketches [{sketch, name, component, part}], kept [{sketch, name, code, reason}]. Each sketch whose plane is an exactly attached face of a part's body goes to that part, as component.move_sketches moves it, and stays where it is on the face; the others (on an origin, construction or fixed plane, on a body of the design itself, or already in their part) stay where they are. One undo step

label: Paste from Another Design
params: component?: where it goes (default: the active one); component_path?: its placement (default: the active one, else its only one); placement?: `world` (default) or `origin`, where copied components go: at the same world coordinates, or with the first one's origin on the target's origin, the others kept where they are from it (bodies always keep their world coordinates). Pastes what was copied in another design: its bodies as imported bodies (no history) in one Import feature, or its components as independent copies with their history, appearances, joints and motion (as `component.paste_new`); the user parameters they use come along, renamed `w_2` when taken. A component that uses what isn't in it (another body, sketch or parameter) is refused, saying what. Returns `bodies` and `feature`, or the pasted components' `paths`

label: Paste New
params: component: independently copy its nested definition graph and history, materials and styles; occurrence?, path?: selected source placement; parent?: component the copy goes in (default: the source placement's; not the component or one inside it); in_place?, parent_path?: as occurrence.copy; translate?: [x,y,z]. Reassigned external bodies become base geometry; retained external links and omitted boundary joints are reported

label: Mass Override
params: component; mass?: kg; com?: [x, y, z] mm; inertia?: [xx, yy, zz, xy, xz, yz] kg m² (omit all to clear): what robot exports use for the component's own bodies

label: Component Physical Properties
params: component?: id or name (default active); descendants?: bool (default true); about?: [x, y, z] (mm). failed is also a view or centre annotation that can't be drawn; an automatic centre mark failure names its view), overridden (a dimension whose text is typed over its value, or a title block cell whose typed text hides a value), out_of_date (a view, a dimension, balloon or note on a view, or a sketch or fill on the sheet, that a deferred drawing shows as it last was), nothing_shown (a view with nothing to measure), empty_field (a title block field with no value, as source.key; label: Export
params: path; format?: stl|stla|obj|step|3mf|3mf-tagged|glb|usd|3dm|urdf|mjcf|sdf|json, or plugin_id.entry for an installed exporter plugin (plugin.list exporters), which writes the whole design with options?: the slot's declared options (default from extension; an extension SolidCraft doesn't write goes to the exporter plugin that claims it; mjcf: the whole assembly as a MuJoCo model, as file.export_mjcf, named by format (a `.xml` path alone is not MJCF); sdf: a Gazebo model folder, as file.export_sdf (the path is the folder, a `.sdf` ending dropped; name?, static?, model_uris?, quality?); docs/sdf.md; 3mf-tagged: 3MF whose triangles carry their B-rep face, at full precision, for meshing and analysis tools; docs/formats/3mf-face-tags.md; obj: the colours of the bodies go in a material library (`.mtl`) written next to the mesh file; glb: binary glTF in metres with Y up, each body placed and named, its colours, metallic, roughness and opacity as materials (a look that is not opaque is alpha blended), and the Glass a render setup gives a body as glTF transmission; Glass with subsurface scattering, Glass two setups give a body differently, or a body a render setup gives an image texture, is refused; urdf: the whole assembly as a robot, with STL meshes written next to it, or where mesh_prefix points with place_meshes; docs/urdf.md; 3dm: Rhino 8, written by cadmpeg: each body where the design shows it (no components), named and in its colour, as its exact shape when every face is planar and every edge straight, else as its mesh, with warnings for what the file leaves out; fcstd is refused, as cadmpeg cannot write a new FreeCAD file yet); bodies?: [names] (JSON, URDF and MJCF export the complete design); writer?: solidcraft|cadmpeg (STEP and IGES only, refused for the other formats; default solidcraft: SolidCraft's own writers; cadmpeg: written from the design by cadmpeg, STEP AP242 with the components and colours but no solid names, IGES 5.3 with each body where the design shows it, named and coloured; warnings say what the file leaves out); urdf only: mesh_prefix? (before each mesh file name, e.g. package://robot/meshes/), place_meshes? (default false: the meshes next to the .urdf whatever mesh_prefix says; true: written where mesh_prefix points, its folder made), effort? (default 1000), velocity? (default 10), mimic? (default false; true: motion links as <mimic>), images?: bool (URDF and OpenUSD, default false, true for OpenUSD with purpose: distribution; true: each shown canvas and decal is written as a textured quad, its image next to the URDF or, for OpenUSD, in the .usdz package, a .usda or .usdc file leaving them out with a warning; an OpenUSD export of chosen bodies writes none, with a warning); quality?: standard|fine|finest (STL, OBJ, 3MF, GLB, OpenUSD, Rhino, URDF and SDF: how closely the mesh follows curved faces, a chord tolerance of 2e-4, 5e-5 or 1e-5 of each body's size; default standard); chord?: mm, 0.001 to 1000 (instead of quality, for the same formats: one chord tolerance for every body; coarser gives fewer triangles); objects?: body|component (3MF only: one object per body, the default, or one object for each placed component with two or more bodies, with those bodies as its parts, so a slicer loads them as one object with parts); lay_on_print_faces?: bool (STL and 3MF only, default false: each body with a print face (body.print_face) is written laid on it, as a slicer export lays it → print_faces: the bodies laid, warnings: each body that has a print face but was written as it lies); solids?: body|face (ASCII STL, format stla only, default body: face writes one `solid <name>` block per B-rep face, named by the face's persistent name, for CFD meshers; docs/formats/stl-face-solids.md); physics?: bool (OpenUSD only, default false: true also writes the joints, gears and racks as PhysX couplings of their joints, the grounded placements, each placement as a rigid body and each component's mass as OpenUSD physics, for a simulator, for the whole design with its components only, else none with a warning; a jointed placement moved without capturing the move is written where its joints place it, with a warning); render_setup?: name (OpenUSD only, default none: the saved render setup whose image textures (base colour, roughness, metallic, and a normal map the file can show as the renderer does) a .usdz package holds on each body's mesh; a .usda or .usdc file is written without them, with a warning; and the optics it gives bodies, written as glass in every encoding: the index of refraction, and full transmission on the MaterialX OpenPBR shader); purpose?: interchange|distribution (OpenUSD only, default interchange: each body's exact shape beside its mesh, for another CAD program; distribution: meshes only, with the pictures shown on the model, for a viewer or a game engine); exact_brep?: bool (OpenUSD only, default true for interchange, false for distribution: each body's exact shape beside its mesh); a given images or exact_brep overrides the purpose's default

(default false; true: motion links as <mimic>); images?: bool (default false) → {path, format, files, links, joints, warnings}: the whole assembly as a robot, with STL meshes written next to it, or where mesh_prefix points with place_meshes; called from a script or MCP it exports as file.export_urdf does; in the app it opens the export's options (mesh prefix, limits, mimic, where the meshes go) first; docs/urdf.md

label: Export Current View as DXF
params: camera: Camera (current view); hidden?: omit|dashed (default omit); tolerance?: 0.0001..1 mm (curve chord tolerance, default 0.01); curves?: lines|arcs (lines, default, writes the short lines the view is built from; arcs writes visible circles and arcs as CIRCLE and ARC); zero?: target|origin (where the drawing's 0,0 is: the camera target, default, or the model origin as seen from the camera); path?: .dxf file (else returns dxf text). Visible placed bodies and shown sketches' profile curves (no construction geometry, points, dimensions or constraints); 2D LINE/LWPOLYLINE entities on VISIBLE/HIDDEN layers (sketch curves on SKETCH), mm; finished sketches are hidden behind bodies, the active sketch is drawn on top; perspective projected onto the camera target plane; no viewport crop or overlays.

label: Insert PCB (Gerber)
params: set?: a board's files as one: a zip, a folder, or any file in the board's folder; each file's layer is found from what it says (Gerber X2, Excellon), the job file (.gbrjob, which also gives thickness and finish) and its name, and outline, drills and layers then name files in the set to use instead; outline: path of the board outline Gerber (RS-274X) layer | outline_text: its text; drills?: path or [paths] of Excellon drill files (up to 16) and/or drills_text?: text or [texts]; thickness?: mm (default 1.6, more than 0, at most 20); name?: the new component's (default: the outline file's name without its extension, or Board); origin?: file (default: keep the files' coordinates) | corner (the lower-left corner of the box around the outline at the origin); layers?: {top_copper?, bottom_copper?, top_mask?, bottom_mask?, top_silk?, bottom_silk?: path of that Gerber layer} and/or layers_text?: the same keys with the layers' text; finish?: hasl (default) | enig, how bare copper looks → {component, component_name, sketch, feature, body, bodies, holes, slots, skipped, thickness, offset: [x, y] added to the files' coordinates, layer_sketches?: ids, prints?: names, warnings}: a new component in the active one, named after the board, holding a sketch Outline on XY with the outline (closed loops inside it are cut-outs) and every hole and slot wholly inside the board, and one extrude of the board by its thickness as the body Board; its properties pcb.outline, pcb.drills and pcb.thickness name the files and the thickness; a hole or slot outside the board or across its edge is skipped with a warning; gaps in the outline up to 0.05 mm are closed with a line and a warning, a wider gap is refused, naming it; each layer given is kept exactly as hidden sketches in the component (Top copper, Bottom mask...) and the board gets each side's printed look (solder mask, copper, finish, silkscreen) as an image on its face, Top print and Bottom print; component properties pcb.<layer> name the layer files. A sketch being edited is finished first. One undo step

label: Insert Mesh
params: path: .3mf, .stl, .obj, .ply (with faces), .glb or .gltf file (its meshes join the design as mesh bodies in a new component named after the file → component, component_name, occurrence; a glTF file's node tree becomes nested components held as one rigid group until component.unlock, a mesh placed again another occurrence, its materials the bodies' appearances, and its metres millimetres); name?; up?: z|y for a glTF file (default y: glTF has Y up, so the import's component is turned a quarter turn about X, Y becoming Z → stand_up: its occurrence; z: the file's axes are kept); units?: mm|cm|m|in|ft for an STL or OBJ file, or a PLY file with faces (default mm): the unit its coordinates are in, scaled to millimetres as the file is read (a 3MF or glTF file states its own). The design keeps the millimetre mesh and not the unit, so insert the file again to try another; origin?: bool (default false: the mesh keeps its file's coordinates; true: once read, scaled and stood up, the import's occurrence is moved so the box around its bodies is centred on X and Y of the active component with its lowest point on Z = 0 → moved_to_origin: [x, y, z], the shift made); crease_angle_degrees?: 0..180 (0 clears imported shading normals for the previous flat-shading behavior; positive angles regenerate angle-weighted normals across manifold edges below this crease angle; omitted keeps authored OBJ normals/smoothing groups, or flat shading when absent; geometry stays unchanged); geometry?: meshes|exact for an OpenUSD file (default meshes: its meshes as mesh bodies, a B-rep with no mesh left out; exact: its exact B-rep where it has one, a BrepArray's solids and shells, comes in as B-rep bodies of an Import feature, as file.insert_step brings a FreeCAD file read with reader: cadmpeg, its prims a product tree, a mesh that only shows a B-rep not read again, and only its meshes with no B-rep as mesh bodies → geometry: "exact"; up and origin work as for its meshes; crease_angle_degrees is refused)

label: Insert STEP
params: path: STEP, IGES, FreeCAD .FCStd or Rhino .3dm file (its bodies join the design as an Import base feature in a new component named after the file, placed in the active component; an assembly's products become nested components, a repeated part one component with an occurrence per placement, all held as one rigid group until component.unlock → component, component_name, occurrence, subcomponents?, rigid_members?: the occurrences its rigid group holds, group?: the folder); folder?: bool (default false; true: an assembly's import, which has subcomponents, goes into a new history folder named `Group #N`); flatten?: bool (default false; true: every solid comes in as a body of the import's own component, with no subcomponents, occurrences, joints or rigid group: a part placed several times is one body per placement where the file places it, and, as no component says which part a body belongs to, its name is prefixed with the outermost named part holding it (`R63: Terminal`), a placeholder name (empty, a bare number, or an exporter's `… STEP translator …`) giving way to its nearest named product's); name? (the feature's and the component's); up?: z|y (default z: the file's axes are kept; y: the file has Y up, so the import's component is turned a quarter turn about X, Y becoming Z → stand_up: its occurrence); names?: auto|solid|product|instance (default auto: keep meaningful solid names, replace placeholders with the nearest named product, else instance; solid: the solid's own name; product: the part's name; instance: the occurrence's name, else the product's); history?: features|solids for a FreeCAD file (default features: its sketches and the Pad, Pocket, Revolution, Groove, Fillet, Chamfer and primitive features that use them are rebuilt as features in the new component, when every one can be and they build what the file holds → features_added, history: "features"; else, or with solids, the file's solids come in as an Import feature, and a warning says why the history was not rebuilt; with features, the file's sketches then come in beside the solids as editable sketches → features_added, history: "sketches"); reader?: solidcraft|cadmpeg for a .step/.stp, .igs/.iges, FreeCAD or Rhino file (default solidcraft: SolidCraft's own STEP or IGES reader, which keeps the STEP text (an IGES file restated as STEP), a FreeCAD or Rhino file's solids restated as STEP by cadmpeg's STEP writer first; cadmpeg: cadmpeg's model read straight into B-rep records, with no STEP text in between, a STEP or IGES file decoded by cadmpeg's STEP or IGES decoder, to compare the two; `flatten` works with either); matrix?: [12 or 16 numbers] (where the new component's occurrence sits in the active component, after `up`: a rigid row-major 3x4 rotation-and-translation or 4x4 matrix, flat or as rows, as occurrence.move takes it, its translation column (entries 4, 8 and 12) numbers or length expressions: one that names a parameter is kept, and the import follows the parameter when it changes (a grounded one stays); a scale, shear or mirror is refused before the file is read); tolerance? (see occurrence.move; envelope?: "box" (also add the import's envelope, a hidden box around every body it placed, in its component, as solid.bounding_solid with `component` makes it → envelope: the body; inspect.clearance and inspect.interference check it instead of the parts with `envelopes: true`)link?: bool (default true: keep a STEP source link for Update Links; false keeps an independent copy; without a disk path the web app keeps a copy);

label: Save
params: path? (default: current file; a name that opens as another kind of file, such as .step, .stl or .dxf, is refused: file.export writes those); format?: container|json (default: json for .json, otherwise container); compression?: fast|compact (default: fast); cache?: bool (the evaluated model, so the design opens without rebuilding; default: true; left out, without waiting, while an imported file's check of its parts still runs); linked_bodies?: bool (the bodies of linked designs and linked STEP files, with a linked design's mesh bodies; false: the file keeps each link without its bodies, opening the design reads them from the linked files again, and a container has no saved model; a link whose file cannot be read now keeps its bodies and is named in warnings; default: as the design was last saved or opened, true for a new design); preview?: bool (saved display meshes, default: false); overwrite?: bool (replace the design's file even though another program or computer changed it since it was opened or saved; without it that save is refused); sign?: bool (the app's own Save only: sign the save with GnuPG, appending a provenance record; container only; a script or agent is refused); signing_key?: fingerprint or user id (default: GnuPG's default signing key) → signature: {method, fingerprint, user_id?} when signed

params: path (a design file name, .sc as a rule; one that opens as another kind of file, such as .step, .stl or .dxf, is refused: file.export writes those); format?: container|json (default: json for .json, otherwise container); compression?: fast|compact (default: fast); cache?: bool (the evaluated model, so the design opens without rebuilding; default: true; left out, without waiting, while an imported file's check of its parts still runs); linked_bodies?: bool (the bodies of linked designs and linked STEP files, with a linked design's mesh bodies; false: the file keeps each link without its bodies, opening the design reads them from the linked files again, and a container has no saved model; a link whose file cannot be read now keeps its bodies and is named in warnings; default: as the design was last saved or opened, true for a new design); preview?: bool (saved display meshes, default: false); overwrite?: bool (as file.save, when `path` is the design's own file); sign?: bool and signing_key? (as file.save, and likewise only from the app's own Save)
