params: path; format?: stl|3mf|3mf-tagged (default from the extension, else stl; 3mf-tagged: docs/formats/3mf-face-tags.md); bodies?: [names] (default: all); ascii?: bool (STL); slicer?: id or name from file.slicers, the program path it lists, or a program the user added under Custom… (send the saved file there, through the same steps as file.send_to_slicer: a slicer that has to be started first is waited for; may be deprecated later in favour of file.send_to_slicer or a Send to App workflow, kept for scripts); single_instance?: bool (default true; see file.send_to_slicer); quality?: standard|fine|finest (STL, OBJ and 3MF: how closely the mesh follows curved faces, a chord tolerance of 2e-4, 5e-5 or 1e-5 of each body's size; default standard); objects?: body|component (3MF only: one object per body, the default, or one object for each placed component with two or more bodies, with those bodies as its parts, so a slicer loads them as one object with parts); lay_on_print_faces?: bool (default false: each body with a print face (body.print_face) is saved laid on it; a file sent to `slicer` is laid on them whatever this says)

label: Send to Slicer
params: slicer: id or name from file.slicers, or a program the user added under Custom…; bodies?: [names] (default: the selected bodies); wait?: block|return|no (default block: a slicer that drops a file at a cold start is started alone and the call waits up to 10 s for it to be ready, then sends; return: start it and answer {starting}; no: send now); single_instance?: bool (default true: PrusaSlicer, SuperSlicer and Cura load the file in the window that is open); format?: 3mf|stl|3mf-tagged (default 3mf, in millimetres; STL if that can't be written); copy_to?: a folder to keep the file in instead (made if missing): it is named after the design with the next free -v<N>, and the reply has `version` and `copy`; copy_overwrite?: bool (default false; with copy_to: one file named after the design, replaced each time) → saves the bodies in this user's slicer folder and opens the file in the slicer. The file name stays the same for the same design and bodies, so sending again replaces it (use the slicer's Reload from disk); with copy_to the slicer opens the file in that folder instead

label: Installed Slicers
params: → the slicers found on this machine: [{id, name, program, icon?}]; pass an id, a name or the program path as file.send_to_slicer's or file.save_mesh's `slicer`

label: Move Design File to Trash
params: path; refuses the current design or its linked files; system Trash only, never permanent deletion

label: Verify Signature
params: path? (default: the design's current file) → {path, status, reason?, truncated, records: [{method, key_id, user_id?, author?, created?, format, covered}]}: status is unsigned, valid, not_covered (signed earlier, saved since without a key), invalid or unsupported

label: End Cap
params: faces: [{face:[x,y,z],body,index,path?}] planar end faces of frame members, picked in world mm (1–256); thickness: length in design units or a parameter expression; offset?: inset of the plate from the outside of the profile, a length; ratio?: the inset as a share of the thickness (give offset or ratio, not both; neither: the plate is flush with the outside of the profile); chamfer?: corner chamfer length along each edge from the corner (default 0; a rounded corner needs at least its rounding); direction?: outward|inward (default outward: past the end; inward: the member is cut back by the thickness and the cap takes its place). One separate body per face, named `<member> End Cap`; the plate is the profile's outer outline on a closed section (tube, pipe, bar), its outside on an open one (angle, channel, beam, slotted extrusion): the edges on the rectangle round the profile with their rounds and chamfers, inward stretches closed along the rectangle. Common name/body_names fields supported.

label: Gusset
params: supports: exactly two {face:[x,y,z],body,index,path?} planar face picks in world mm; leg1, leg2, thickness: lengths in design units or parameter expressions; relief?: inside-corner setback along each leg (default 0); clip?: equal-distance clipping at both outer tips (default 0: triangle); offset?: signed distance along the joint from the centre of the faces' overlapping span (default 0); placement?: center|positive|negative (default center). Ordered outward support normals define the positive joint/thickness direction by their cross product. Contact strips must fit entirely on both finite faces. Creates a separate body, named `Gusset`, `Gusset (2)`… unless body_name is given; does not join, drill or add a weld. Common name/body_name fields supported.

label: Frame Member
params: sketch?: the frame sketch (id or name; 2D or 3D); lines?: [curve ids] (one member each; default: every straight line drawn in the sketch: not construction, not projected or otherwise linked, not of no length); pairs?: [{a, b}] (one straight member from point a to point b each, after the lines' members, found again whenever the design changes; a and b are point references: {vertex: [x,y,z]}, {sketch, point} (a 3D sketch node as `wire:index`), {construct_point: name}, a snap point or the origin, as saved ({type, …}) too; typed coordinates are not points here; each pair is named pair1, pair2… and a pair's id is never given again; Edit Feature gives back the pairs it keeps with their `id` and `next_pair`, and an `id` without `next_pair` is refused); give `sketch`, `pairs` or both; continuous?: bool (default false; one member along explicitly selected lines and circular arcs in connected tangent path order, curves reversed as needed, stable member id `$path`; corner None only, without overrides, Fit Ends, Coped, Flip, gap or point pairs); profile: {kind: bar|round_bar|rect_tube|round_tube|angle|channel|i_beam, …its dimensions: each a number in the design's units or a length expression over its parameters ("tube_wall", "2 in"); a channel's flange_slope is an angle (a number of degrees)} (frame.profile.list gives each kind's dimensions and an example; dimensions left out take defaults from the profile's size) | {size: a standard steel size by name, such as "RSC 203x89", "PFC 200x90x30", "RSA 50x50x5", "SHS 100x100x5", "RHS 200x100x6.3" or "CHS 42.4x3.2" (frame.profile.list lists them), alone: it brings its dimensions} | profile_sketch: a sketch whose profile is the section, in its own x and y around its origin, with profiles?: picks as solid.extrude takes them (default: its material, nested loops alternating, so two circles make a tube); anchor?: origin|center|centroid|top_left|top|top_right|left|right|bottom_left|bottom|bottom_right (the profile point that sits on each line, default origin); locate?: [x,y] (the profile point that sits on each line, in mm from the profile's own origin: a bar's or an angle's bottom-left corner, a channel's web back at mid-height, the centre of other profiles; takes precedence over `anchor` and keeps the member attached at that point when the profile size changes); corner?: auto|none|mitre|butt (how members ending at one point are cut; default none); flip?: bool (a butt's other member runs through); fit_ends?: bool (fit free ends to earlier Frame Members' tubes; default false); coped?: bool (cut every butt joint to the other tube's real shape, radii kept: butts, ends on a tube's middle, crossings, overlaps and fitted ends, mitres left as they are; not under none; default false; an older `coped_butt`, the frame's or an override's, reads as butt with coped); corners?: [{members: [2 to 1000 line or pair ids, or {line}], kind: auto|none|mitre|butt, gap?: length expr}] (that corner's, crossing's or overlap's own type, and its own weld gap; the members in order: the first runs through a butt, or stays whole at a crossing or overlap, and of three or more the first two make the corner; an older script's `corner` reads as `kind`, and its `flip` is saved as the order today's rules give with the first two swapped; an overlap takes no gap); gap?: length expr (the weld gap at every welded end, 0…1000 mm, default 0: each mitre plane half of it back, a butting or fitted end, a crossing's pieces' included, that far off the member it meets; through members keep their length, overlaps are notched without it); angle?: angle expr (the profile turned about the line; default 0: its y as near world up as the line allows, a vertical member's x along world X); up?: X|-X|Y|-Y|Z|-Z (the world axis that is up for the profile, default Z; a part drawn with Y up takes Y, so its members need no angle and lines along Y are its vertical members, their x along world X, or world Y when X is up); mirror?: bool (the profile mirrored across its y axis); name?; body_name? (what the members are named after, then numbered: `Rail`, `Rail (2)`…; default the size's name, `RSC 203x89`, the profile's description, `Rect Tube 40x40x3`, or the profile sketch's name); names?: {line or pair id: name} (names to keep, as Edit Feature keeps them). One body per line or pair, from its start to its end; each member keeps its name when other lines or pairs are added or deleted. Returns the feature and the bodies it made

label: Multi-Trim Corner
params: feature: the Frame Member (id or name); members: [2 to 1000 line or pair ids, or {feature?: the frame's own name, line}] (a corner, crossing or overlap of the frame, the members in order: the first runs through a butt, or stays whole at a crossing or overlap, and of three or more the first two make the corner); kind?: auto|none|mitre|butt (default auto: the frame's own type, with this order); flip?: bool (the first two in the order today's rules give them, swapped; without it the members are saved as given); gap?: length expr (this corner's weld gap, 0…1000 mm; default the frame's; an overlap takes none); remove?: bool (take the override of these members away, back to the frame's own rules; no kind, flip or gap with it). Replaces the override of the same members (any order) or adds one, as one undo step; the frame stays one timeline entry. Returns the edited feature as frame.member does

label: Mounting Plate
params: face: [x,y,z] on a planar support face (world mm); body?, index?, path?: exact face pick; shape?: rectangle (default) | round; width,height: rectangle length expressions | diameter: round length expression; thickness: positive length expression; offset?, x_offset?, y_offset?: signed length expressions, default 0; angle?: angle expression, default 0; holes?: {pattern: none} (default) | {pattern: rectangle, diameter, pitch_x, pitch_y} (four holes) | {pattern: circle, diameter, pitch_diameter, count: 2…128, angle?}. A mounting/base plate or bolted end flange, kept as a separate body centred on the current face's area centroid, extending along its outward normal; holes must be inside its perimeter and separate. Does not drill the support. name?, body_name?, body_names?, participants? (ignored)

disabled_reason: no sketch is being edited (Create Sketch or Edit Sketch first)
label: Insert Profile
params: profile: {kind: bar|round_bar|rect_tube|round_tube|angle|channel|i_beam, …its dimensions: each a number in the design's units or a length expression over its parameters ("tube_wall", "2 in"); a channel's flange_slope is an angle (a number of degrees)} (frame.profile.list gives each kind's dimensions and an example; dimensions left out take defaults from the profile's size) | {size: a standard steel size by name, such as "RSC 203x89", "PFC 200x90x30", "RSA 50x50x5", "SHS 100x100x5", "RHS 200x100x6.3" or "CHS 42.4x3.2" (frame.profile.list lists them), alone: it brings its dimensions}; at?: [x,y] (sketch mm, default the origin); anchor?: origin|center|centroid|top_left|top|top_right|left|right|bottom_left|bottom|bottom_right (the profile point placed on `at`: its origin, the default and a built-in profile's centre, its bounding box's centre, its centroid, or a corner or edge middle of its bounding box); angle?: radians, counter-clockwise; fixed?: bool (default true: the curves are locked, so solving the sketch keeps the shape); sketch?: id|name (default: the sketch being edited). Returns the section as frame.profile.properties does. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Profile Library
params: family?: RSC|PFC|RSA|SHS|RHS|CHS (list only that family's sizes). Returns kinds: [{kind, label, required, optional, example}]: the built-in profiles, each SolidCraft's own parametric definition; and sizes: [{family, kind, standard, source, names, additional?}]: the standard steel sizes by name, each family with the published table its dimensions come from (frame.profile.properties with {profile: {size}} gives a size's dimensions and section)

label: Profile Properties
params: profile: {kind: bar|round_bar|rect_tube|round_tube|angle|channel|i_beam, …its dimensions: each a number in the design's units or a length expression over its parameters ("tube_wall", "2 in"); a channel's flange_slope is an angle (a number of degrees)} (frame.profile.list gives each kind's dimensions and an example; dimensions left out take defaults from the profile's size) | {size: a standard steel size by name, such as "RSC 203x89", "PFC 200x90x30", "RSA 50x50x5", "SHS 100x100x5", "RHS 200x100x6.3" or "CHS 42.4x3.2" (frame.profile.list lists them), alone: it brings its dimensions}; density?: kg/m³ (adds mass_per_m, kg/m). Returns profile (every default filled in), area (mm²), centroid [x,y] (mm, from the bounding box centre), ixx, iyy, ixy (mm⁴ about the centroid), width, height

label: Remove Tube
params: members: [{feature: id|name, line: the tube's line or pair id}] (1…1000, all of one Frame Member). Takes those tubes out as one undo step: a pair goes from the feature's pairs, a sketch line from its lines (the line stays in its sketch; a feature on every line of its sketch lists the others from then on), and the corner overrides that name a tube taken out go too. Taking out the last tube deletes the Frame Member. Returns the edited feature as frame.member does, or {deleted: the feature's name}

label: Rotate Member
params: face: {face:[x,y,z],body,index,path?} a face of the frame member to turn, picked in world mm; angle: the angle the member is turned to about its own line, counter-clockwise looking back from the line's end (an angle or a parameter expression; 0 = as the Frame Member laid it, turned about the profile's centre). Adds a step after the Frame Member. parallel_to?: a straight edge, a sketch line ({sketch, curve}) or an axis: the angle is worked out once so the picked flat side ends up parallel to it (the nearest turn, within a quarter turn of the member's current one), and only that angle is stored, not the line; it wins over `angle` when both are given. Common name field supported.

label: Trim/Extend
params: members: [member…] (the members to trim or extend: each a member's body name, or {feature: the frame member feature (name or id), line: its line's id}); to: [target…] (or one target: what each member's end is trimmed or extended to: a member (its body name, or {member, side?: right|left|top|bottom of its profile; default the side the trimmed member meets}): a butt joint against that side, worked out from its line and profile so it follows edits; or {plane: XY|XZ|YZ|a construction plane|{origin, normal}|{face: [x,y,z]} a planar face}, or {plane_ref} a plane as the design saves it, as Edit Feature keeps it); end?: auto|start|end (which end of each member moves; default auto: for each target the end nearer it); gap?: length expr (the weld gap between each end and its target, default 0, at most 1 m). Each member's end that meets a target is rebuilt flat against it (a slanted face cuts it at a slant); a member keeps its body and name. Members changed by later features are refused as members or member targets; use a planar face target for a modified body. Every member must meet a target, and two targets may not move the same end. Returns the feature and the bodies it changed

label: Accessibility Analysis
params: direction?: [x,y,z] the tool comes from (default Z, from above); clear?: true turns the analysis off

label: View Analysis
params: off?: true turns the view analysis on now off. → active: the command id of the view analysis on (inspect.zebra, inspect.draft, inspect.curvature_map, inspect.environment_map, inspect.accessibility, inspect.continuity, inspect.isocurve or inspect.curvature_comb), or null. One is on at a time: turning one on turns the one on before off. Read-only without `off`

label: Center of Mass
params: bodies?: [names] (default all): the centre of mass (uniform density) of each and of all together, from the exact mass properties `inspect.measure` takes → center, volume, bodies: [{body, center, volume}], skipped: [{body, reason}] (bodies that enclose no volume or could not be measured)

label: Classify Points
params: body: name; points: 1–256 world-space [x,y,z] in mm; face?: face name or point on a face → results in input order: {class: inside|outside|on}; on also gives face (persistent name) and normal (outward unit vector). Exact trimmed geometry at the body's modelling tolerance; mesh bodies refused. At shared edges/vertices, face selects the normal, otherwise the first containing face in model.faces order

label: Clearance
params: bodies?: [names] (default: every solid body, in world placement, but those in `against`; mesh bodies are not measured); against?: [names] (only pairs with one body in `bodies` and the other here); min_volume?: mm³ (default 0.01: smaller overlaps count as contact); clearance?: mm (default 0: report pairs closer than this); nearest?: n (each body of `bodies` gets its n nearest others); skip_within?: "occurrence" (pairs of bodies of one occurrence) | "component" (pairs of bodies inside one placed component, its subcomponents included) | null; envelopes?: bool (default false: component envelopes, solid.bounding_solid with `component`, are left out unless named; true: each is checked instead of the bodies inside it, and a body named inside one means it; an envelope is never paired with a body inside it); tolerance?: mm (default 1e-6: a gap below it is contact, 0) → overlaps: [{a, b, volume_mm3, area_mm2, bbox, center}]; near: [{a, b, distance_mm, from, to, overlap_mm3?: a contact's shared volume below min_volume, exact?: false when measured on the meshes}], nearest by body (the same for pairs that overlap: 0); nearest: {body: [{body, distance_mm}]} (omits pairs in unchecked); unchecked: [{a, b, reason, distance_mm?, exact?}] (pairs whose overlap could not be worked out, with non-boolean minimum distance when computable and exact: false when measured on the meshes; each mesh body, STL/3MF/OBJ import, is not measured and is listed as {a: name, b: null, reason: "mesh body: not checked"}, also when named in `bodies` or `against`; the result's `bodies` counts the solid bodies only); pairs_checked; pairs_reused (of those, measured by an earlier call: neither body changed or moved since); pairs_pruned (ruled out by their boxes); ms. Distances are measured on the exact faces and edges, the meshes only rule pairs out

label: Component Colors
params: enabled?: bool (omitted: toggle); temporary component colours, without changing appearances

label: Compare Bodies
params: a, b: body names (default: the two selected bodies, or the design's only two), in world placement; tolerance?: mm (0.001 to 10, default 0.01): surfaces closer than this agree; spacing?: mm (default 0.5): the largest piece of a face sampled as one point, coarser for a body that would need more than max_points? (default 8 million, up to 50 million) samples; max_regions? (default 50); color?: true | {only_in_a?, only_in_b?: "#rrggbb"} (colours the faces that hold a region, red where only a has material and green where only b has: the faces mostly beyond the tolerance, else the one with the largest share; an undo step) → a, b: volume_mm3, area_mm2, center_of_mass, bbox; difference: b − a; deviation: a_to_b, b_to_a (max_mm, mean_mm, at, area_beyond_mm2); regions, largest first: side (only_in_a | only_in_b), volume_mm3, center and bbox (measured_by: "boolean": exact, the pieces of a − b or b − a there, measured as inspect.measure does; "not measured": the cut could not be made, so volume_mm3 and center are null and not_measured says why, never an estimate), area_mm2, max_deviation_mm, at, faces_a, faces_b (face indices, as model.faces lists them); identical; verdict; warnings (a body whose surface does not enclose what it measures, lines left out, a cut that could not be made). The regions are found from the two surfaces, so near-identical bodies compare too

label: Compare Picture
params: reference: path to a PNG or JPEG the model should match; view?/camera?/bodies?/rows? as inspect.silhouette; crop_px?: [x, y, w, h] in pixels, or crop_fraction?: [x, y, w, h] as fractions 0..1 of the picture (to take one view off a board); part_fills_crop?: false — with true the crop box is the part itself and no background search runs, for a crop that tightly frames the part; fit?: "width" | "height" | "both" (default "width"): one uniform scale, taken from the named dimension ("both" claims both and scales by width, reporting aspect_mismatch when the shapes differ); overlay?: a .png file to write the overlay to (red model, blue picture) → overlap (0..1), edges: top|bottom|left|right in mm at nine stations (positive where the model reaches past the picture, null where a station misses one of the two), the grid and its mm_per_px, and overlay: the file written, when asked for. The compare is outline only: holes are not compared — both the picture's and the model's holes are filled

label: Continuity Analysis
params: body?: name (default: the visible bodies); edges?: [x,y,z] points or {"index": i} (default: every edge of the body; a pick must match one body); samples?: 3…257 stations along each edge, ends included (default 33); gap_tolerance_mm? (default 0.001), angle_tolerance_deg? (default 1), curvature_tolerance_per_mm? (default 0.01), curvature_change_tolerance_per_mm2? (default 0.001), curvature_change_rate_tolerance_per_mm3? (default 0.0001); add?: true keeps the seams already shaded and adds these (measuring an edge again replaces it); clear?: true turns the analysis off. → each edge's worst gap (G0), normal angle (G1), curvature jump (G2), jump of the curvature's change across the seam dκ/ds (G3) and of that change's rate d²κ/ds² (G4), from the faces' exact derivatives, as {value, at: [x,y,z], edge_fraction}; its order (g0…g4: the highest every station meets within the tolerances, null where the faces do not meet), its verdict (smooth: g2 or better, curvature_jump, sharp or gap) and a summary; the seams are shaded in the viewport

label: Curvature Comb Analysis
params: curves?: [sketch curve ids] (sketch?: id|name, default active) | edges?: [[x,y,z] points on body edges: the edge whose exact curve passes nearest] | faces?: [[x,y,z] points on faces] with count?: isoparametric curves each way (default 4; combs along the face's iso grid); density?: teeth per curve, 2…2000 (default 40; on an edge or an iso curve exactly that many, evenly spaced along its parameter); scale?: comb length per unit curvature (default auto: the longest tooth a fifth of the combs' size); length?: a multiplier on the automatic scale, 0.01…100 (default 1; ignored with `scale`); add?: true keeps the combs shown and adds these, every comb again at one scale (with nothing picked it draws those shown again with this call's options, or turns the analysis on with none); clear?: true turns the analysis off. Every comb of a call shares one scale, so tooth lengths compare across curves; the viewport draws them. The curvature is exact: from each sketch curve, edge curve (line, circle, ellipse, B-spline, NURBS, intersection curve) or face surface's own derivatives, never from the display mesh; a face's teeth are the surface's normal curvature along each iso curve, along the surface normal. → combs: [{curve, teeth: [[foot, tip]], envelope: [tip], max_curvature, min_radius}] (those shown, with `add`), scale

label: Curvature Map Analysis
params: radius?: mm shown red (default: a tenth of the model's size); clear?: true turns the analysis off

label: Draft Analysis
params: pull?: [x,y,z] direction (default Z); angle?: degrees (default 1); clear?: true turns the analysis off

label: Environment Map Analysis
params: clear?: true turns the analysis off

label: Find Hole Stacks
params: bodies?: [names] (default all but standard parts); diameters?: [[min, max]] (mm; holes and slot widths in any range); slots?: bool (default true: obround slots count); touching?: mm (largest gap between layers, default 0.05); axis_tolerance?: mm (largest offset between hole axes, default 0.1) → stacks: [{axis (unit, from the start into the stack: −z for a vertical stack), start, end: [x,y,z] on the axis, grip_mm, layers: [{body, d_mm, t: [t0, t1] (mm from start), slot?: {length_mm, along}}]}] (two or more bodies each); lone: [{body, d_mm, at, axis, depth_mm, slot?}] (holes in no stack). Standard parts' bodies count only when named in `bodies`

label: Interference
params: bodies?: [names] (default: all, in world placement; a name that is no body is refused); budget_s?: seconds (default 240, at most 86400: pairs not finished by then are listed in unchecked as "not checked: the time budget … ran out" and the call returns); exclude_pairs?: [[a, b]] (pairs left out, such as a pin in its hole: each side a body's world name or an occurrence id|name, matching every body under it; pairs_excluded counts them); envelopes?: bool (default false: component envelopes, solid.bounding_solid with `component`, are left out unless named; true: each is checked instead of the bodies inside it, and a body named inside one means it; an envelope and a body inside it are never paired, counted in pairs_excluded) → interferences: pairs that overlap with the overlap volume, area, bounding box and centre, and a_part, b_part: {component, path: [occurrence names], path_ids} where each body sits (also on unchecked pairs); unchecked: [{a, b, reason}], the pairs that could not be checked, with the reason, and each mesh body (STL, 3MF or OBJ import: not intersected) as {a: name, b: null, reason: "mesh body: not checked"}, so count: 0 is not read as no overlap (checked counts the solid bodies). Bodies are pruned by bounding box first, then by their display meshes (pairs whose meshes stay apart by more than their chord tolerances, neither inside the other, are clear without a boolean), so any number of bodies is fine; the pairs left are intersected exactly, in parallel on desktop, the slowest first; at most 20000 pairs whose boxes overlap are intersected per call (truncated: true and skipped_pairs: n say when more were left out). Also: pairs_candidate (boxes overlap), pairs_cleared (by the meshes), pairs_intersected, pairs_not_checked, pairs_excluded, budget_exceeded, threads (worker threads; 0: on the calling thread), boolean_ms and tessellate_ms (kernel time summed over the pairs), slowest: [{a, b, ms, boolean_ms, tessellate_ms}] and ms

label: Isocurve Analysis
params: faces: [[x,y,z]…] points on faces (1…100); count?: whole number of curves each way, 1…100 (default 8); add?: true keeps the faces already shown; clear?: true turns the analysis off. → each face's isoparametric curves, u = const and v = const of its surface, evenly spaced across it and cut to its trims, as points (`curves`) and per face (`faces`); the viewport draws them

label: Measure
params: bodies?: [names] (default all); within?: {min:[x,y,z], max:[x,y,z]} (world mm); mode?: intersects|inside (default intersects, includes touching); names_only?: bool (each world body's name and its definition's, nothing measured) → closed per body; volume_mm3, center_of_mass, density_g_cm3 and mass_g only for closed, consistently oriented bodies; area, bbox and counts for all; total.open_bodies_skipped counts bodies excluded from volume/mass totals; or items: [1-2 selections] (face/edge: type, body, and point on it or index from model.faces/model.edges, or both) → length/area/volume; a face's perimeter_mm, with outer_perimeter_mm and inner_perimeter_mm on a flat face with holes; diameter, radius, circumference or arc_length/angle_deg of circles, arcs and cylinders; slot sizes; min (distance_mm, from, to), max, center_distance (centre to centre, or from an axis) and angle

label: Minimum Radius Analysis
params: curves?: [sketch curve ids] (sketch?) | edges?: [[x,y,z]…] | faces?: [[x,y,z]…] (default: every face of every body); the smallest radius of curvature of each and where it is

label: Parameter Sweep
params: parameter: name; values: [number | expression] (at most 200) | from, to: numbers, steps? (default 10, at most 199: steps + 1 values) → for each value, in a copy of the design (the design itself is not changed): {value, ms (the rebuild), ok, failed: [{feature, name, error}], warned: [{feature, name, warning}] (features that build at the current value and fail or warn at this one), joints_lost: [{joint, name, origin?: a|b, why}], joints_flipped: [{joint, name, origin: a|b, degrees}] (an origin's z turned more than 90° on its own part from where it is now), sketches_flipped: [{sketch, name, degrees}] (the sketch plane's normal turned more than 90°), sketches_failed: [{sketch, name, failing, folded}] (a solve that fails, or keeps a triangle's turn or an offset's side only by flipping it)} (or {value, ms, ok: false, error} where the parameter takes no such value); summary: {values, ok, slowest_ms, failed, joints_lost, joints_flipped, sketches_flipped, sketches_failed} (how many values show each)

label: Compare Parameter Variants
params: variants: [{name, set: {parameter: number | expression}}] (1 to 12; up to 16 existing parameters each). Rebuild each set together in a separate copy of the open design. Returns baseline and ordered results with volume, mass, body counts and rebuild regressions. No edits are kept.

label: Section Analysis
params: plane: XY|XZ|YZ | construction plane name or id | {origin, normal}; offset?: expr, how far the cut moves against the plane's normal as given (before any flip), so a positive distance cuts more away: into the part from a face's outward plane (XY: -Z, XZ: -Y, YZ: -X; negative moves it the other way); at?: expr, the cut's world coordinate on the named plane's axis (XY: Z, XZ: Y, YZ: X), instead of offset; flip?: bool (hide the other side; the plane stays where it is); hatch?: bool (hatch the cut faces, in each body's colour; default true, or as it was with add or replace); add?: bool (add the plane to the section, starting one if there is none, instead of replacing it: each plane hides what lies on its positive side, so the section keeps only what every plane keeps, a quarter for two square planes; at most 6 planes, hidden ones included; the new plane takes the lowest id no plane has); replace?: a plane's id (move that plane to `plane`, keeping its id and the others; a hidden one is shown); or remove: a plane's id (take that plane out; the last turns the section off); or hide / show: a plane's id or [ids] (a hidden plane stays in the section and cuts nothing until shown); or folder: false (hide the Analysis folder: the planes on show stop cutting and come back with folder: true; while it is hidden, hide and show change only which planes come back, and a plane added or moved shows it again, with them); or clear: true (all planes). Each change is one undo step; the design is untouched. Returns section: the plane made {id, origin, normal, hatch, and for a named plane axis and at} (null when the section is off, or for remove, hide, show and folder), planes: [{id, origin, normal, hidden}], every plane of the section by id, and folder: null, or while the folder is hidden the ids that come back with it

label: Delete Saved Section Analysis
params: section: a saved section's name; the section on show stays as it is

label: Rename Saved Section Analysis
params: section: a saved section's name, name: the new one

label: Save Section Analysis
params: name: what to call the Section Analysis on show (its planes, hidden ones too, and its hatch); a saved section of that name is replaced. Saved with the design

label: Show Saved Section Analysis
params: section: a saved section's name; it replaces the section on show, so the planes follow it. One undo step

label: Silhouette
params: view?: front|back|left|right|top|bottom|iso (default front); or camera?: {target: [x,y,z], yaw, pitch, distance, fov?} (mm, radians; fov 0 means parallel); bodies?: [world body names] (default visible bodies, named hidden bodies included); rows?: mask height in pixels (default 240, clamped to 16..1024) → tightly framed run-length mask, box_mm, mm_per_px, right/up, projection, body and triangle counts

label: Zebra Analysis
params: stripes?: number across the view (default 12); clear?: true turns the analysis off

label: As-Built Joint
params: type, a: occurrence, b: occurrence (stay where they are); at?: joint origin (default: b's origin) — the joint's frame; one on a or b is kept on its face or hole there, so the joint follows it as the design changes; name?; limits?: [[min, max] | null…]; quiet?: bool

label: Cam
params: a: the cam's joint (revolute); b: the follower's joint, a slider (a translating follower) or a revolute (an oscillating one),          b driven by a; profile: {sketch: id|name, index?: the profile (default: the largest)} | {edges: [[x,y,z]…] (points on edges of          the cam's bodies forming one closed loop, world), occurrence?}: the cam's outline, in a plane square to its axis, read again          whenever the design changes; follower?: knife|roller|flat (default knife; flat: a face square to a slider's line); radius?: the          roller's radius (mm, an expression or {circle: [x,y,z], occurrence?}: the roller's round face, which is its tip too); tip?: a          joint origin where the follower touches: its knife's point or its roller's centre, such as {circle: [x,y,z]} on the roller          (needed for an oscillating follower; a translating one's line runs through it, by default along its slider's axis); flip?: bool (ride the cam from the other side          than the one the follower is on now); link?: index (replace that motion link; profile, follower, radius and tip left out then keep that cam's definition, picked profile and round face included, and flip left out keeps the side it rides from now) → link, lift: {min, max, rise, unit} (b's travel          over a turn of the cam), reverse (the side it rides from), follower_offset (mm: how far a translating follower's line passes          from the cam's axis); b keeps where it is, also when the link replaces another (at the current pose)

label: Joint
params: type: rigid|revolute|slider|cylindrical|pin_slot|planar|ball, or a relation: parallel|perpendicular|angle|point_on_plane|point_on_line|line_on_plane (ties only some directions or points, made where the parts are; several between two parts add up); a, b: joint origins ({occurrence, face|circle|edge|point: [x,y,z] in world, or face|circle: "<face name>", plane: "XY"|"o:<ids>/origin/<item>"|"<name>", axis: "Z"|"o:<ids>/origin/<item>"|"<name>"; z? for a point, end?, x? as joint.origin} | origin name); values?: [angles in deg or expressions, distances]; limits?: [[min, max] | null…]; flip?: bool (default false: the origins are mated, b's z against a's as two faces meet - two plane or axis datums mate aligned, each part keeping its side of the datum, and flip mates them; true: b's z along a's, so two origins given at one point with the same z and x stay as they are; a point origin without x takes its x from z, so give x on both, or use joint.as_built, to keep a turned part where it is); offset_x?, offset_y?: lateral mm in a's frame or an expression the joint follows; offset?: mm or an expression; angle?: deg or an expression (an angle relation's tilt from mated; for other joints the default is none, or a half turn where that turns b less, so faces that already meet stay as they are); name?; quiet?: bool (leave out dof and fixed). An expression for offset, angle or a value is kept with the joint and worked out again whenever the design changes, so the joint follows the parameters it names; a joint whose expression no longer works out (a parameter deleted) is left out of the solve with the reason in its errors

label: Delete Joint
params: joint: id|name (or origin: name, link: index)

label: Drive Joints
params: joint: id|name; value | values: [angles in deg or expressions, distances] (values not given keep theirs; a value driven drops the expression joint.create gave it; clamped to the limits; the other joints of a closed loop follow, and the motion stops where the loop can no longer close → stopped_by_loop); quiet?: bool (leave out dof and fixed) → values: [{name, value, unit: deg|mm, limits}] as joint.list gives them; requested: the values asked for, in the same form; held: [{name, requested, value, unit, why}] for each driven value that ended up elsewhere (a motion link sets it, as a screw's travel follows its turn; a limit; contact; a closed loop); moved: whether any occurrence moved; reason: why the joint can move nothing (suppressed: nothing is stored; its origins lost; its chain joined to nothing grounded → unconnected: the occurrence named; or, when nothing moved, the first held value's why); index?: zero-based coordinate to drive with value (the other coordinates follow); continuous?: bool (drag frame, suppress UI echo); stop_at_budget?: bool (default false: a contact check past its sample or work budget fails the drive; true: the drive stops at the last placement checked clear → stopped_by_budget {budget: samples|work|intersections, fraction})

label: Joint Dynamics
params: joint; index?: value index (default 0); effort?: N or N m; velocity?: m/s or rad/s; damping?: N s/m or N m s/rad; friction?: N or N m (omit all to clear): what a simulator reads, written by URDF export; the joint solver does not use them

label: Edit Joint
params: joint; a?, b?: joint origins as joint.create takes them (a side left out keeps its place; the two must stay on different occurrences); type?, flip?, offset_x?, offset_y? (plain joints only; a number, or an expression the joint then follows), offset?, angle? (a number, or an expression the joint then follows), suppressed?, name?; the joint re-solves, keeping its limits and expressions (a relation's values start again where its parts are); an edit that places it again (not a rename alone) meets a loop it closes as joint.create does, turning an angle a half turn where only that meets it

label: Find Joint Limits
params: joint: id|name; index? (one value; default every value); refine?, step?, occurrences?, against?, contact_sets?, exclude_pairs? (as joint.sweep) → values: [{index, dof, unit, value (now), min, max, min_by, max_by, range}], each value swept both ways from where it is, its own limits ignored, closed loops following; each side stops at the first contact (bisected to `refine`), where a loop cannot close, or at another limit (another value's, or another joint's through a motion link): min_by/max_by {a, b, at} | "loop" | "limit" | "budget" (its work ran out: the last value checked clear) | "turn" (an angle with no contact within a turn: a turn from the other side, or ±180° from now when nothing is met at all) | "range" (a distance with no contact within the parts' reach: min/max null); touching_at_start, overlapping_at_start: [{a, b, depth_mm}] (already passing into each other: they stop it only going deeper), refine_mm, gap_method, gap_tolerance_mm, pairs (0: no two parts to check, so nothing is swept). The design is not changed

label: Gear
params: a, b: joints that turn (revolute), b driven by a; ra, rb: the gears' pitch radii (or tooth counts): mm, an expression, or {circle: [x,y,z], occurrence?}: the round face there, its radius (read again whenever the design changes, so the ratio follows edits); internal?: bool (one is a ring gear: both turn the same way; by default b turns the other way); reverse?: bool; link?: index (replace that motion link; a radius left out then keeps the old gear's, picked round face included) → link, ratio (b's degrees per a's); b keeps where it is, also when the link replaces another (at the current pose)

label: Inspect Joint
params: joint?: id|name (default: every joint, narrowed by the filters joint.list takes: kinds?, exclude_rigid?, exclude_rigid_groups?, moving_only?, occurrences?; omitted?: what they left out) → joints: [{id, name, type, suppressed, visible, flip, offset (mm), offset_xy: [x,y] (mm), angle (deg), values: as joint.list gives them, dofs, expressions?: {offset?, angle?, values?}, a, b: {occurrence, occurrence_name, component, component_name, path (occurrence names from the top, `/` between), snap (as saved: type, pick, face, end, edge, corner, x, point, z, in the component's coordinates), references: [{role: face|end|x|edge|corner, name, role_in_feature?: (top, side:c1…), feature?: {id, name, type} (the feature that made the face; error when it is gone), sketch?: {id, name, curve, curve_type} (a face swept from a sketch curve), faces?: [an edge's two faces], unverified?: a name saved before exact names}], resolves, frame?: {origin, z, x} in the world, error?: why the origin is lost}, links: [{index, role: driver|driven, …as joint.list}], errors, conflicts}] (reads only: nothing changes)

label: Joint Limits
params: joint; index?: value index (default 0); min?, max? (numbers, or expressions the limit then follows as the parameters change; omit both to clear)

label: List Joints
params: quiet?, filters (a joint is kept when it passes every one given): kinds?: [types], exclude_rigid?, exclude_rigid_groups? (the rigid joints holding a component's contents together, as an imported assembly's placements), moving_only? (no rigid or suppressed joints), occurrences?: [id|name] (an end at one of them or inside one; dof narrowed to them too); dof_free_only? (dof lists only occurrences that can still move); summary? → joints (type, occurrences, values, limits, offset_xy: [x,y] in mm; expressions: {offset_x?, offset_y?, offset?, angle?, values?} when they were typed as expressions), origins, links, degrees of freedom, conflicts, floating: [{occurrences, joints}] (joint chains joined to nothing grounded: the solver places none of them, so driving them moves nothing), omitted?: {joints, by_type, floating, dof} (what the filters left out), summary?: {joints, by_type, suppressed, rigid_groups: [{component, name, joints, members}] (the 20 largest), more_rigid_groups?: {groups, joints}}

label: Motion Link
params: a, b: joints; ratio (b = ratio · a + offset): b's units per a's (mm per deg for an angle driving a distance); offset?: in b's units (deg for an angle, mm for a distance, or an expression); ia?, ib?: value indices (default 0); link?: index (put this link in place of that motion link, as the gear and cam commands do) → link: the link's index, as joint.list numbers them

label: Joint Origin
params: name?, export_frame?: bool (robot exports write it as a frame of its own), occurrence?: id|name (default: from the pick, or the named face's component), path?: [occurrence ids from the root] (the placement picked on, ending at the occurrence: a part in a sub-assembly placed more than once is then on that copy; default: the occurrence's first placement, or with no occurrence the placement nearest the pick), face: [x,y,z] | "<name>" (centre of a planar face) | circle: [x,y,z] | "<name>" (centre of a round end: a point on its wall or rim, the end's centre, or the round face's name as model.faces lists it) | edge: [x,y,z] (a point on an edge of a planar face: the edge's middle, z out of the face, y into it; on?: [x,y,z] a point on the face (default: the larger planar face beside the edge); corner?: [x,y,z] near one end: the corner there, x and y along its two edges into the face; found again by name, so it follows the face as it changes size; z?: [x,y,z] the frame's z instead of the face's normal, along the edge when it runs that way, x chosen from z: an edge or corner picked as it is, kept as a point where it can't be found by name) | point: [x,y,z], z?: [x,y,z] | plane: "XY"|"XZ"|"YZ"|"o:<ids>/origin/<item>"|"<name>" | axis: "X"|"Y"|"Z"|"o:<ids>/origin/<item>"|"<name>"; a circle's z?: [x,y,z] (a round edge's centre with the way out of it: its end by name when that is the frame it shows, else a point there); body?: the named face's body; end?: "<name>" (a circle's end: the face across its rim there; default the end nearer the pick); x?: [x,y,z] (a direction, world) | "<face name>" | {face: [x,y,z]} (the frame's x: a direction, a plane's normal, or the way to another hole's axis; keeps a round origin's turn; a point's x is a direction, laid square to its z, default: chosen from z alone). Faces are kept by name: the origin follows its face, and a circle its end, when the design changes

label: Export Origin as Frame
params: origin: a named joint origin; frame: bool: robot exports write it as a frame of its own (a tool tip, a sensor mount)

label: Rack and Pinion
params: a, b: a joint that turns (revolute: the pinion) and one that slides (slider: the rack), in either order, b driven by a; radius: the pinion's pitch radius (mm, an expression, or {circle: [x,y,z], occurrence?}): the rack travels radius × the turn in radians; reverse?: bool; link?: index (replace that motion link; the radius left out then keeps the old pinion's, picked round face included) → link, ratio (mm per degree, or degrees per mm); b keeps where it is, also when the link replaces another (at the current pose)

label: Reach Point
params: occurrence: id|name; point: [x,y,z] (where its point goes, world); at?: [x,y,z] (its point, in the world where it is now; default: the centre of          its bodies' box); z?: [x,y,z] (the way its axis then points); axis?: [x,y,z] (that axis, in the world now; default: its own z); joints?: [ids          or names] (only these move toward the point; the other joints of a closed loop they are in follow); quiet?: bool; continuous?: bool (a frame          of a drag: the answer says continuous, and the app's command line doesn't echo it). Moves the values of the joints          on its chain from where they are to the nearest pose, within their limits, through motion links, keeping closed loops closed as joint.drive does;          with contact sets on, they stop where two parts of a set would pass into each other; from?: [{joint, values}] (the values those joints start from instead of the design's, as joint.list gives them: the pose a drag's last frame showed; with contact sets on, refused unless every value is already the design's) → reached; error_mm (and error_deg with z): how close it got; point: where its point is; values: [{joint, name,          values}] of the joints that moved, as joint.list gives them; moved; stopped_by_limit: [{joint, value, limit: min|max}]: the limits it rests on          short of the point; stopped_by_loop: {joint}: the closed loop that stopped it (its chain alone gets closer); stopped_by_contact: the pair of a contact set that stopped it, as joint.drive says; reason: why nothing can move

label: Rigid Group
params: occurrences: [ids or names] (move together, as they are)

label: Screw
params: joint: a cylindrical joint (its turn drives its travel) | a, b: a joint that turns and one that slides, b driven by a; pitch: travel per turn (mm or an expression); reverse?: bool (a left-hand thread); link?: index (replace that motion link; the pitch left out then keeps the old screw's) → link, ratio (mm per degree, or degrees per mm); b keeps where it is, also when the link replaces another (at the current pose)

label: Solve Joints
params: re-place the occurrences from the joints; quiet?, dof_free_only? (dof lists only occurrences that can still move; omitted.dof counts the rest) → conflicts, errors, dof

label: Sweep Joint
params: joint: id|name; from, to: its value the sweep runs between (degrees for angles, mm for distances, or expressions); index? (which value, default 0); step? (between samples, in the joint's unit; default: fine enough that no part passes through another between two); refine?: mm (the first contact is bisected until no part moves more than this between the last clear value and the touching one; default 0.01); occurrences?: [ids or names] (checked against each other; default every occurrence), with against?: [ids or names] (the parts that stay: each of `occurrences` only against these), or contact_sets?: true (the pairs of the design's contact sets); exclude_pairs?: [[a, b]] (occurrences by id or name: pairs of bodies under a and b are not checked, such as a pin in its hole); budget_s?: seconds (at most 86400; past them the sweep stops with what it found; its work is then not capped. Without it the work caps, 4096 samples, 64 bisection steps and 500 million triangle tests, stop it the same way); report_gaps?: bool (the nearest gap at every sample, default false); apply?: bool (leave the design where the sweep stopped; default false: the design is not changed) → stopped_at (the last value clear of contact, or where a loop or limit stopped it; null: it reached `to`), stopped_by: {a, b, at: [x,y,z] (where they touch, world), a_part, b_part: {component, path: [occurrence names], path_ids} (where each touching body sits)} | "loop" | "limit" | "budget" (stopped_at: the last value checked clear) | null, samples: [{value, min_gap_mm?, pair?, parts?}], min_gap? (report_gaps: {part: {mm, at_value, to}}, the nearest each part came to another), unit, gap_method ("mesh": distances between the tessellations), gap_tolerance_mm (how far those can be off: 0 when every face is flat), pairs (checked), touching_at_start: [[a, b]] (pairs already touching at `from`, such as parts joined face to face or a door on its frame: these stop it only once they pass into each other deeper than they start), touching_parts (where their bodies sit), budget_s, budget_exceeded, budget_ran_out: "time" | "samples" | "bisections" (a contact reported less refined than `refine`) | "intersections" | "work" | null, applied. The parts are tested at the samples and through the bisection; the motion is on a copy (closed loops follow, contact sets do not stop it)

(2…1000, default the study's steps + 1); budget_s?: seconds (above 0, at most 86400; default a fixed work budget): the time the check may take instead, looked at between samples, for a mechanism such as a gear train that needs longer → collisions: [{a, b, first_step, last_step, steps: [[from, to]…] (the step ranges where they overlap), volume_mm3 (the most volume they share at a sample, worked out exactly from the bodies), deepest_step (the first sample sharing that volume), not_measured (null, or why the volume was not worked out at every sample they overlap, such as a budget it ran past: then volume_mm3 and deepest_step are null, never an estimate), depth_mm (how far into each other at most: an estimate from points of the bodies' contact meshes, not exact)}], clear (every sample checked and none collide; never while truncated), pairs (checked), samples (taken), truncated (the work budget, or budget_s, ran out; checked_to: the last step checked), budget_s (when given), stopped_at, stopped_by_loop. EXR requires an opt-in raw linear master retained by that completed CPU or GPU job; never converts PNG pixels.
