Blocked calibration and external-sun rigs refuse. Returns a geometry-clearance review requirement; does not create cards or modify the scene.

label: Save Surface Binding
params: name: CPU or GPU setup; set?: setup patch; surface: same input as render.library.surface.prepare; replace?: false. Pins exact source hashes and definition/feature/occurrence identity with local-mm mapping in one undo. No paths, mesh ordinals or physical material changes.

label: Prepare Authored Surface Maps
params: id: SURF-*; body_index and body_name from render.scene; origin?:[0,0,0]; plane?:xy/yz/zx; scale?:1; rotation_rad?:0 (positive around the plane normal). Returns an explicit GPU temporary planar binding and a source usable by saved CPU/GPU surface.bind, with source hashes, original millimetre scale, image-up normal orientation and absolute base-color semantics. No document change; height/displacement and true anisotropy are not included.

label: Remove Surface Binding
params: name: setup, target: saved definition/feature/component/occurrence_path, set?: setup patch. Removes only that explicit binding in one undo; no device or current geometry required.

label: Find Render Library Targets
params: query?: exact-name substring; offset?:0; limit?:128 (1..128). Returns a bounded page of captured body ordinals/names, revision and scene bounds. Settles the model through ordinary command handling; never returns a large mesh payload.

label: Add Light
params: name; id except add; settings?: full unsaved RenderSetup; expected_revision?:u64; set for set/add: kind directional/point/spot/area, intensity_ev, temperature_k, softness, azimuth_deg, elevation_deg, distance_mm, size_mm, aim_at, width_mm, height_mm, position_mm, direction, edge_u_mm, edge_v_mm, radiance, colour, reference_distance_mm, minimum_distance_mm. Validated finite light edit in one undo. Existing family caps and backend support apply; refusal is atomic. Names remain defaults.

label: Duplicate Render Light
params: name; id except add; settings?: full unsaved RenderSetup; expected_revision?:u64; set for set/add: kind directional/point/spot/area, intensity_ev, temperature_k, softness, azimuth_deg, elevation_deg, distance_mm, size_mm, aim_at, width_mm, height_mm, position_mm, direction, edge_u_mm, edge_v_mm, radiance, colour, reference_distance_mm, minimum_distance_mm. Validated finite light edit in one undo. Existing family caps and backend support apply; refusal is atomic. Names remain defaults.

label: List Render Lights
params: setup?: saved setup name OR settings?: complete RenderSetup snapshot; neither uses defaults. Returns {lights:[{id,kind,name,name_key,number,implicit,intensity,colour,...spatial fields}]}. IDs are kind:zero-based-source-slot, stable across numerical edits but not family changes/reordering/removal/rig replacement; point and spot share punctual slots. Includes implicit default/preset lights. GPU RGB radiance is factored as colour * intensity; area edges are full world-mm vectors. Read-only, no host, camera change, save, render, model evaluation or undo. See docs/render-settings.md.

label: Mute Light
params: id: kind:slot light address; mute:bool. Validates and echoes per-document UI view state, applied to live preview and captured render copies only. Never changes saved settings or history.

label: Remove Render Light
params: name; id except add; settings?: full unsaved RenderSetup; expected_revision?:u64; set for set/add: kind directional/point/spot/area, intensity_ev, temperature_k, softness, azimuth_deg, elevation_deg, distance_mm, size_mm, aim_at, width_mm, height_mm, position_mm, direction, edge_u_mm, edge_v_mm, radiance, colour, reference_distance_mm, minimum_distance_mm. Validated finite light edit in one undo. Existing family caps and backend support apply; refusal is atomic. Names remain defaults.

label: Set Render Light
params: name; id except add; settings?: full unsaved RenderSetup; expected_revision?:u64; set for set/add: kind directional/point/spot/area, intensity_ev, temperature_k, softness, azimuth_deg, elevation_deg, distance_mm, size_mm, aim_at, width_mm, height_mm, position_mm, direction, edge_u_mm, edge_v_mm, radiance, colour, reference_distance_mm, minimum_distance_mm. Validated finite light edit in one undo. Existing family caps and backend support apply; refusal is atomic. Names remain defaults.

label: Solo Light
params: id?: kind:slot light address; solo:bool. Enabling requires an id; false clears solo. Validates and echoes per-document UI view state. Never saves settings, evaluates geometry, opens an editor or changes history.

label: Save Optical Binding
params: name: CPU or GPU setup; set?: complete numerical setup patch; body_index and body_name: exact captured target; expected_revision; optics:{ior,absorption_per_mm:[r,g,b],boundary:closed_mesh|closed_box|thin_sheet,thickness_mm,shadow_transmission,subsurface?:{scattering_per_mm,anisotropy},model?:{roughness:0..1,dispersion?:{abbe_number:5..200},thin_film?:{ior:1..3,thickness_nm:0..100000}}}; replace?:false. The optional model adds isotropic rough transmission, three-band dispersion and one lossless coherent film. CPU models require explicit Path; rough sheets require straight transmitted shadows off. See docs/render-glass-material-models.md. Stores stable definition/feature/occurrence identity in one undo without modifying engineering geometry/materials. CPU Path consumes at most 128 certified optical targets; the legacy non-Path producer retains eight. Without options.path, sheets and axis-aligned boxes retain the existing transport. Explicit progressive options.path enables exact closed-mesh certification, bounded nested convex-parent media, Beer/Snell/Fresnel and thin transmitted shadows; touching or unproven boundaries and closed transmitted-shadow connections refuse explicitly. Existing subsurface parameters may be consumed on certified closed Path media with denoising explicitly off; scalar free-flight/HG walks and separate Beer absorption are supported without refracting-boundary next-event approximation. A zero scattering rate preserves transport. GPU nested media require separate job.options.nested_media and producer certification. Unresolved or incompatible targets refuse atomically.

label: Remove Optical Binding
params: name: saved setup; target: exact saved definition/feature/component/occurrence_path; expected_revision. Removes only that optical assignment in one undo without a device or file access.

label: Set Render Output Size
params: width, height: 1..16384; custom?: bool. Validated Render output draft request; headless echo only, no design edits or job. The UI separately limits new selections to 8192 per side, 33554432 output pixels and the selected rendering profile.

label: Check Render Request
params: setup?: saved name OR settings?: full RenderSetup. A typed job selects raster/cpu_raytrace/gpu_path and its numerical options plus embedded HDR before dispatch; only replace and transient studio_weights may accompany it. Without job, the legacy runtime controls below remain available. See docs/render-settings.md. studio_weights?: three finite 0..1 visibility weights for raster or implicit GPU studio sources only; never saved. integrator?: raster (default) or raytrace; progressive?: false (registered GPU path, CPU integrator/LED options are mutually exclusive); texture_filtering?: false (GPU); CPU raytrace.texture_filtering?: false. Explicitly enables ray-footprint mip and bounded anisotropic map filtering on GPU, and bounded anisotropic filtering on CPU. GPU filtering off retains bilinear LOD0; CPU filtering off retains isotropic mip selection, using the coarsest available mip when footprint data is unavailable. samples?: 1..65536; max_depth?: 1..64; seed?: u32 for progressive; raytrace?: bounded runtime progressive/primary_samples/lights/punctual_lights/area_lights/area_samples/seed/exposure_ev/shadows/reflections/anisotropic_faces/emissions/surface_effects/dielectrics/environment options, only with raytrace. CPU raytrace.lens?: {aperture_radius_mm:0..10000000,focus_distance_mm:0.000001..1000000000}; positive aperture requires explicit CPU progressive sampling and a bounded perspective camera; absent/zero keeps the original CPU ray stream. See docs/render-thin-lens.md. CPU raytrace.volume?: one HomogeneousVolume box with world-mm min_mm/max_mm, extinction_per_mm:0..1000, RGB scattering_albedo:0..1 and anisotropy:-0.95..0.95. Positive extinction requires explicit Indirect lighting and cannot combine with Glass/SSS or surface Denoise. Physical eye/pupil prefixes and the orthographic line/box union preserve camera/model framing under existing ray/profile caps. See docs/render-cpu-volume.md. CPU raytrace.sun? uses the shared finite-disk Sun contract; raytrace.sky? uses {gradient,rotation_rad,intensity}. Both require explicit Indirect lighting, and gradient Sky excludes a constant/HDR environment. Their medium NEE uses the HG response/PDF and physical light source; see docs/render-cpu-celestial.md. CPU transparent_background?:false exports straight-alpha primary geometry coverage for fixed/progressive sampling; body/face opacity must remain 1, and active bloom/backdrop/photographic effects require opaque output. CPU raytrace.output?: {tone_map,finishing,backdrop,linear_exr}; shared presentation supports up to 8192 per side and 33554432 output pixels, CPU exposure remains raytrace.exposure_ev; raw FLOAT32 EXR is retained only at final completion. CPU raytrace.budget?: compact (legacy default), studio or workstation; see docs/render-cpu-resource-profiles.md for explicit image/geometry/memory/work limits. CPU raytrace.progressive?: {samples_per_pixel:1..profile limit, seed:u32}; requires primary_samples:1 and selected reflections.samples:1; area/LED sources and certified planar anisotropy/thin-sheet/axis-aligned-box dielectric continuations share the existing bounded transport and compatibility checks. See docs/render-cpu-progressive.md; environment?: {path: scoped HDR, expected_sha256?: inspected digest, rotation_radians: 0, intensity: 1, samples: 16} OR {resource: saved HDR digest, rotation_radians, intensity, samples}; embedded resources cannot combine with path/hash; explicit sRGB/D65 HDR primaries required. Opaque CPU preview with selected mirror/rough-specular reflections and certified planar anisotropy. HDR with rough reflections or anisotropy requires fully metallic selected bodies and all effective faces; unsupported combinations refuse. Optional raytrace.path:{max_depth:1..64} enables CPU diffuse/specular GI with matched rectangle/HDR light and BSDF MIS plus certified closed-mesh Glass. It requires explicit progressive camera sampling, primary_samples:1 and traced shadows; selected reflections and certified anisotropy refuse before HDR IO without changing intent. CPU Path dielectric subsurface?:{scattering_per_mm:0..100,anisotropy:-0.95..0.95} enables homogeneous free-flight/HG walks inside certified closed media; positive rates require denoising off. Contained light connections include scattering survival; closed refractive light connections and combining Glass with external volume remain unsupported. Absent path keeps the old certified thin_sheet/closed_box producer and refuses subsurface intent explicitly. See docs/render-cpu-general-glass.md and render-raytrace-dielectrics.md. CPU emissions are visible radiance and may light neighbors through sampled Path continuation, without mesh-emitter next-event sampling; surface_effects change roughness/shading normals without geometry changes. led_strip?: continuous world-mm LED rectangle recipe; led_samples?: 1/4/16/64 for the whole strip, default16. At most8directional+8punctual+4rectangle/LED sources; shared area N. See docs/render-light-union.md. transparent_background?: false; replace?: false. With progressive:true, raytrace instead accepts GPU dielectrics/clear_coats/textures; environment instead accepts tagged hdr/embedded_hdr/sky with rotation_rad/intensity; file hdr supports expected_sha256, embedded_hdr uses a document resource digest. See docs/render-hdr-resources.md. GPU lens, studio lighting, tone_map, denoise, clamp_indirect?: 0.000001..1000000 (biased; caps each contribution from the first bounce on, keeping its hue; see docs/render-path.md), bounded finishing/backdrop and linear_exr retention are also available. CPU raytrace and GPU top-level controls accept supersampling:1|2 (default 1; doubles internal width and height at 2, averages scene-linear premultiplied samples before tone mapping, exports selected dimensions), denoise_settings:{passes:1..3,strength:0..1,firefly_suppression:bool,optical_filter:bool}, and denoise_diagnostics:false. Optical filtering defaults to true for eligible mirror/glass guides; optical_filter:false restores legacy opaque-only display denoising. Guides and diagnostics retain their independent eligibility policy and conservative highlight protection. CPU raytrace.threads:0..64 selects bounded automatic workers at 0 (default), serial work at 1 or an explicit count from 2 through 64. Resource checks include internal image buffers and worker scratch. See docs/render-quality-controls.md. Both path tracers accept optional metal_energy_compensation: true for rough isotropic metals (inside CPU raytrace or top-level GPU). Both methods accept optional caustics {photons:1..1048576,radius_mm:0.000001..1000000,max_depth:1..64,seed:u32,area_lights?:false,environment?:false,guided_emission?:false,refresh_per_pass?:false} (inside CPU raytrace; top-level GPU). Optical assignments accept optional model {roughness:0..1,dispersion?:{abbe_number:5..200},thin_film?:{ior:1..3,thickness_nm:0..100000}}. CPU advanced models require Path; rough sheets require straight transmitted shadows off. See docs/render-glass-material-models.md. GPU adaptive?: {pilot_samples:16..256,min_samples:16..samples,relative_error:0..1,absolute_error:0.000001..1000000,coverage_error:0.001..0.25} allocates independent production budgets; pilots are discarded, not a certified error guarantee. transmission_samples?:1|2|4 stratifies the first Fresnel branch with extra path cost. volume?:{min_mm:[x,y,z],max_mm:[x,y,z],extinction_per_mm:0..1000,scattering_albedo:[r,g,b],anisotropy:-0.95..0.95} is one finite homogeneous world-mm medium; active media require explicit lighting/environment and refuse glass, denoise and multiple transmission strata. These fields also persist in GPU job.options. See docs/render-materials/TRANSPORT-MASTER-BATCH-2026-10-23.md; see docs/render-transmission.md, render-environment.md, render-runtime-textures.md, render-thin-lens.md, render-studio-lighting.md and render-denoise.md. Optional CPU raytracing requires a raytrace-cpu build and native host, checked before scene capture. Stale geometry is rejected. See docs/render-jobs.md

label: Copy Render Check Report
params: text: nonempty report, at most 65536 bytes. Validated clipboard request; headless echo only, never renders or edits a design.

label: Apply Native Studio
params: Same reviewed input as render.preset.resolve, expected_revision required, replace_lighting_and_environment:true and replace_stage:true when an existing stage would change. Re-resolves the complete candidate and publishes one undo or no mutation; camera, optical bindings, geometry and engineering materials are preserved.

label: Review Native Studio
params: id: NATIVE-STUDIO-001..025; name; set?: typed CPU/GPU setup patch; expected_revision?:u64. Resolves original built-in HDR/rig/passive ground with conservative geometry clearance, returns all replacements and preserved fields without mutation. Unbound SCENE-* concepts are not accepted.

label: Review Fixed Sampling Budget
params: id: Q-*; variant:fixed_samples_png for the existing GPU projection, or cpu_progressive_png for Q-001/002/003 CPU cost budgets; acknowledge_omissions:true. Optional cpu:{minimum_budget:compact|studio|workstation,adaptive?:captured AdaptiveSampling} selects the smallest existing profile admitting pilots plus production without lowering minimum_budget. CPU budgets use authored sizes, 16/32/64 production samples and seed21026; preserve transport depth, denoise, optics and effects. Read-only numerical projections, not convergence/time guarantees or complete quality acceptance. Never switches executor, adopts fixed CPU sampling or mutates a shot.

label: Close Render Image
params: No parameters. Return to Model Preview; headless echo only, never cancels a job.

label: Copy Render Image
params: job?: completed JobId (default selected result). Validates the retained PNG for app clipboard copying (max 4096 per side, 4194304 pixels); headless returns frame metadata only. Never copies a provisional image or starts a job.

disabled_reason: no completed render results are retained
label: Discard Render Result
params: index: integer 0..7, oldest first; must be retained. Drops only that transient result, selecting the newest remaining result if necessary; echoes index.

label: Retain Displayed Render Result
params: job?: completed JobId (default selected result), or null to clear selection. Selects within the eight retained completed results; oldest is evicted first. Preserves exact export bytes and original host memory accounting. No design/undo change; preview or foreign jobs refuse.

label: Regrade Linear Master
params: job?: exact completed JobId (default selected result); presentation: {exposure_ev?,tone_map?,finishing?,backdrop?,background?,transparent_background?}. Queues cancellable nondestructive PNG presentation from that retained native FLOAT32 master, not from PNG. Captured geometry/camera/lighting and source EXR remain unchanged; no path tracing, denoising, external EXR import or automatic file writes. Returns a distinct job with source identity and original-master digest. Existing frame retention and export rules still apply.

disabled_reason: no completed render results are retained
label: Select Render Result
params: index: integer 0..7, oldest first; must be retained. Selects a completed result as transient per-document view state; echoes index.

label: View Render Image
params: view: model|image|fit|actual|denoise_mask. Guide-mask view requires a selected completed result captured with denoising diagnostics. Validated result canvas request; headless echo only, never starts a job.

label: Inspect Render Scene
params: No parameters. Authoritative product-scene metadata, without modelling overlays or mesh payloads. Explicitly settles stale geometry; does not render an image. See docs/render-workspace.md

label: Apply Render Camera
params: name: saved setup. Applies its existing Camera snapshot including roll/up as view state, without modifying the document or starting a render.

label: Save Render Settings with HDR
params: name, set: typed CPU/GPU setup patch with hdr/environment unset; path: scoped HDR; expected_sha256?: digest returned by render.hdr.inspect (changed sources refuse); rotation_rad?:0, intensity?:1; samples?:1/4/16/64 for CPU only (default16); assume_linear_srgb?:false for GPU only. Captures immutable bytes and saves resource plus setup atomically in one undo, without a host; returns name/setup/resource metadata, never source bytes

label: Render Settings
params: name?: saved setup. Without name returns {setups, defaults}; with name returns {name, setup}. Does not evaluate the model or apply a camera. See docs/render-settings.md

label: Save Render Settings
params: name: setup name, set: object of fields to replace (backend, mode, camera, width, height, format, exposure_ev, environment_rotation, environment_intensity, background, job, surfaces, optics, coats, stage). job?: typed active raster/cpu_raytrace/gpu_path configuration with optional validated embedded HDR reference; omitted preserves, null clears, object replaces the complete job. Creates from defaults and saves without a host, validates atomically, one undo step; identical edits are no-ops. See docs/render-settings.md

label: Duplicate Render Shot
params: name, new_name, expected_revision:u64. Copies exact saved setup and resource references in one undo. Existing destinations refuse; captured jobs and camera navigation are unchanged.

label: Remove Render Shot
params: name, expected_revision:u64. Removes only that saved setup in one undo; retains resources, geometry and captured results.

label: Rename Render Shot
params: name, new_name, expected_revision:u64. Renames exact saved setup in one undo; an existing destination or stale review refuses.

label: Save Physical Render Background
params: name: typed raytrace setup, set?: setup patch, kind: floor_wall or cyclorama, reflectance_linear?: [0.18,0.18,0.18], expected_revision: reviewed revision, replace_stage?:false. Fits a finite floor/wall or a 24-strip polygonal cyclorama behind the visible subject using the saved camera azimuth; world +Z up and a minimum one-mm stage envelope. Preserves subject geometry, lighting, output, pose and engineering materials; one undo and rechecked product separation. Not an infinite/analytically smooth/terrain background.

label: Remove Render Stage
params: name: setup, set?: setup patch. Removes saved render-only panels atomically; CAD geometry and lighting are unchanged.

label: Save Render Ground
params: name: typed raytrace setup, set?: setup patch, margin_fraction?:0.25, gap_mm?:0.1, reflectance_linear?:[0.18,0.18,0.18], replace_stage?:false. Fits one finite passive ground below the visible product once and saves its physical transforms in one undo. Product AABB separation is rechecked on every render.

label: Render Image
params: Same request as render.preflight. Captures an immutable product scene and queues a bounded image job. Returns its session-scoped job identity, captured scene_generation and progress. Does not change the design. See docs/render-jobs.md

label: Render Progress
params: job?: {session, serial, generation}. Non-blocking progress, errors and captured frame metadata with queue:{running,waiting,job,shot,error}. Without job returns queue only. Advances an explicitly started render.batch through render.start as jobs finish; never pumps render work. Preview is separate from the exportable final image.

label: Import Surface Maps
params: name; set?: typed CPU raytrace or GPU path setup patch; body_index and body_name from render.scene; frame: world-mm origin/u/v physical repeat vectors; maps: explicit base_color_srgb/normal_opengl/roughness_linear/metallic_linear {path,expected_sha256?}; provenance:{author,source,license}; normal_strength?:1; flip_v?:false; replace?:false. Captures exact PNG/JPEG bytes and saves definition-local binding in one undo. CPU maps require noninterlaced 8-bit PNG. Saved designs reopen without the source files.

label: List Embedded Surface Images
params: No parameters. Lists bounded design-owned texture digests, byte counts, dimensions, declared provenance and referencing setups; never returns image bytes or source filesystem paths.

label: Remove Embedded Surface Image
params: sha256: exact embedded image digest. Refuses while any saved setup uses the image, listing its users. Removing an unused image is one undo step.

label: Select Boundary
params: body?: world body name, faces?: face indices of it (default: the selected faces, else the last selected body), holes?: bool, add?: bool → selects the edges that bound exactly one face of the set (exact topology), outer loops only unless holes (a hole: a walk of the faces' inner loops only); a body alone gives its free edges → selected, body, edges, loops, holes_left

label: Select Edge Loop
params: body?: world body name and edge?: edge index, together (default: the last selected edge), face?: which of the edge's faces, add?: bool → selects the closed loop of edges of that face that holds the edge (exact topology); without face: a flat face, then one with more than one loop, then the lowest index → selected, face, edges

label: Selection filter
params: mode: body|face|component → validated UI pick granularity; headless echo only, no document edits or undo

label: Invert Selection
params: no parameters → in place of the selected faces, edges or bodies, the other faces or edges of their bodies, or the other shown bodies; a body selected with some of its faces or edges inverts inside it; other items stay selected

label: Selection Mode
params: mode: faces|bodies|features|parts|components|sketch → mode; what a click on the model picks: faces, edges and vertices, the face's whole body, the feature that made it, the innermost placement or the top-level component holding it, or sketch geometry only. A window setting: the design is untouched

label: Select Same Look
params: body?: world body name, face?: face index; defaults to the current body/face selection → selects objects using the resolved appearance

label: Select
params: items: [{type: body|edge|face|feature|sketch_curve|sketch_point|profile, …} or {type: drawing, drawing, object: ids of the drawing open and of a view, dimension or balloon of it}], add?: bool; face/edge: body plus point [x,y,z] in world mm or index (both also accepted); a point uses Measure's pick tolerance, an index supplies a point on the item; invalid partial picks leave the selection unchanged

label: Select Sharp Edges
params: angle_deg?: 1…179 (default 30), body?: solid body name (default: every shown solid body), add?: bool → selects the edges whose faces' normals turn by more than angle_deg, measured on the exact surfaces; tangent edges never

label: Delete
params: items?: [selection items]; components?, occurrences?, canvases?, point_clouds?, joints?: [ids or names]; preserve_projection_link?: bool (default false, passed to sketch.delete including dry_run); dry_run?: bool → deleted, deleted_joints, would_fail, skipped (one undo step). With a drawing open, items are its views and annotations ({type: drawing, drawing, object}); each view takes its annotations with it; a view with views projected or cut from it is refused, naming them, unless they are in items or contents: delete takes them too → views, dimensions, balloons, notes, centre_marks, centre_lines, sketches, fills: [the ids that went], deleted: the names of the views that went with those asked for

label: Get Selection
params: detail?: bool (default true: resolve each item's geometry) → {count, items: [{kind (= type: body|face|edge|vertex|feature|sketch_curve|sketch_point|sketch_midpoint|sketch_constraint|profile|plane|axis|construction_point|occurrence…), the selection's own fields as select.set takes them (body, index, point, id, sketch, path…), and with detail: face: name (persistent face name), name_exact, surface ({type: plane|cylinder|cone|sphere|torus|other, normal/point, origin/axis/radius…}), area_mm2, planar; edge: name (persistent edge name), curve (line|circle|arc|other), length_mm, start, end, center/axis/radius for round edges; body: volume_mm3, feature, visible; any body item: component {id, name} and occurrence_path in an assembly; sketch items: sketch (its id, as select.set takes it), sketch_name, entity (line|circle|arc|point|midpoint|…), position for points and midpoints}]}; read-only, [] when nothing is selected

label: Apply Settings Profile
params: name → name, applied, skipped: [preference]; switches every setting the profile holds at once

label: Delete Settings Profile
params: name → deleted

label: Export Settings Profile
params: name, path?: file → profile (a `solidcraft-profile/1` document), written to `path` when given; never opens a dialog

label: Import Settings Profile
params: path: file | profile: `solidcraft-profile/1` document, name?: 1..64 characters → name; adds the profile without switching to it

label: Settings Profiles
params: → profiles: [name], active: name|null; handled by the app

label: Rename Settings Profile
params: name, to: 1..64 characters → name

label: Save Settings Profile
params: name: 1..64 characters → name; keeps the current input and interface settings under `name` (replacing a profile of that name) and makes it the active one

label: Bead
params: sketch? (default: active or last sketch) + curves: straight sketch lines on a face of a planar panel of a sheet, one bead along each (its ends where the end ramps meet the face); depth, width: expr (on the side it stands out of, width between the flanks' virtual sharps); angle?: expr (flanks, default 45 deg) | crown_width?: expr; base_radius?, crown_radius?: expr (inner, default: the rule's bend radius); end_length?: expr (each end's ramp, default 3 x depth); margin?: expr (warns nearer than this to edges, cut-outs, bends and beads; default 3 x thickness); shape?: trapezoid; flip?: bool (out of the other face); body? (default: the one sheet whose planar panel the first centreline lies on) - formed beads (stiffening ribs) that keep the sheet's thickness: in the folded solid, listed in the flat pattern (beads) and drawn in the DXF (FORM_UP / FORM_DOWN); the flat blank stays flat

label: Convert to Sheet Metal
params: body (a solid or a surface body); rule?; bends?: [[x,y,z] on sharp edges]. (#6748) surfaces become the rule's sheet, its thickness, radius and reliefs whatever the body's: every face of the body but skip?: [faces left out, as points or names], each a panel however thin the body (a thin plate is six panels; sheet.recognize reads a body that is sheet metal already as one sheet); or, with face?: [x,y,z] on a face or its name from model.faces, and faces?: [more faces], those faces and every face a bend joins to them. No face is fixed. A cylinder or cone is a roll at its own radius, and a bend modelled with its radius is a bend (pick it on its roll); every sharp edge between two faces of the sheet is cut open with the rule's gap but the `bends`; a ring of bends is refused; the faces' holes become cut-outs, but engrave?: [the walls and floor of a recess in a face] makes that recess a pocket of the face's panel, as deep as its floor lies; panels whose material would overlap are refused, naming them; direction?: inside (default) | outside (the side of the faces the material lies on). The body becomes the folded sheet, and sheet.flat_pattern shows its flat

label: Export Bend Table

the smallest used is returned as `radius_applied`, each edge's as `radii_applied: [{edge: [x,y,z], radius}]`, and noted in the feature's warning; taper: along each straight edge between planar faces where it doesn't fit, the radius follows the room there as a smooth spline, down to 0 where a face closes to a point, noted in the feature's warning)

label: Hole
params: position: [x,y,z] on a face of a body (numbers, or length expressions the hole follows; a position on no face is refused: the hole starts at that face, its depths are measured from it, and material above it (a body over it, a taller wall beside it) is left standing) | sketch + points: [sketch point ids] (one hole each, perpendicular to the sketch, into the material on whichever side of the sketch plane it is) | sketch alone (every sketch point: standalone points and circle centres); flip?: bool (sketch points: drill to the other side); single?: bool (with one sketch point: a Single hole that follows the point, drilled into the face there); direction?: [x,y,z], each a number or an expression with no unit ("-sin(t)") the hole follows as the parameters change (default: into the face, against its outward normal; where faces of several bodies meet there, the face of a body in `targets`; one that leaves the face is mirrored into it; ignored with sketch points unless single); diameter | thread (a tapped hole, drilled with the tap maker's tabulated drill: ISO metric (a custom metric size: major minus pitch), UNC/UNF, G, Rp, Rc 1/16 to 4, NPT 1/16 to 3; a `diameter` given with it chooses another drill, from the thread's minor diameter to 5% over the tap maker's) | clearance: "M6" with fit?: close|normal|loose (ISO 273); head?: "ISO 4762" (socket head) | "ISO 7380-1" (button head) | "ISO 10642" (countersunk head) (with clearance: the recess the screw's head sits in. A cap screw's: a counterbore, so type defaults to counterbore; its diameter is the head's dk plus head_gap each side, its depth the head's k plus head_gap; a cb_diameter or cb_depth given keeps its value. A countersunk head's: a countersink, so type defaults to countersink; 90° unless cs_angle is given, its diameter the head's dk plus head_gap each side, so the head sits head_gap below the face; a cs_diameter given keeps its value); head_gap?: length (default 0.5 mm; an expression with parameters is kept, so the recess follows them); depth? (default through all; from where the hole starts, not from `position`: the face it enters, or for a sketch point inside a body the sketch plane) | to?: [x,y,z] (To Object: drill to that face or point); references?: [{edge: [x,y,z] on a straight edge of the face, distance: expr}] (at most two; the centre goes that far from each edge's line, in the face's plane, and follows the edges; with a numeric position only); type?: simple|drilled|counterbore|countersink; tip_angle?; cb_diameter?, cb_depth? (from where the hole starts, as depth), bridge?: length (counterbore: two 3D-printing bridge layers this thick below its floor, a slot along X then a square; e.g. 0.2 mm); cs_diameter?, cs_angle?; thread?: "M6", "1/4-20 UNC", "G 1/4", "Rp 1/4", "Rc 1/4" or "1/4-18 NPT" (cosmetic unless modeled); hand?: right|left (the tapped thread's hand; default right; needs thread); thread_class?: the tapped thread's tolerance class, saved for drawings and changing no geometry (ISO metric: 6H, 5H, 7G, or a pitch and minor diameter class such as 5H6H; UNC/UNF: 1B, 2B or 3B; G, Rp, Rc and NPT take none; needs thread);thread_depth?: positive length independent of drill depth (default: full useful cylindrical wall; must fit that wall); modeled?: bool (needs thread: the tapped thread cut into the wall, the groove between its teeth, as solid.thread's modelled one; default false: listed only); ease_out?: expr|standard|short (modelled tapped threads: the inner end, towards the bottom, fades out over this length, ISO 3508's runout, standard 2.5 P, short 1.25 P; without it the groove stops square at thread_depth, or clear of a blind hole's bottom); targets?: [body] (the bodies to drill; holes at the points of a sketch on a body's face default to that body, found along the holes' direction on it alone; explicit targets or participants override, ["*"] every body); old_surface_start?: bool (sketch points: a point inside a body starts the hole at the body's surface whatever plane the sketch lies on, as designs saved before #11538 drilled; set on those holes, keeps them as they were when edited)

label: Loft
params: sections: [{sketch, profiles?} | {sketch, point: id} (an apex)] (2…50, in order; matching hole counts, no holes at an apex); rails?: [{sketch, curves: [ids in order]}] (1…16 guide rails from the first section to the last, through every section's outline: the loft follows them between the sections, passing through every rail; not with sections that have holes; one or two to an apex); rail_fit?: scale|stretch (one or two rails; with three or more it has no effect: each section is warped between them to pass through them all; default scale: with one rail the sections grow evenly with the rail's distance from their middle, with two with the distance between the rails; stretch: only that way); operation?, touching?, targets? (Join excludes hidden bodies from automatic targets; explicit targets or participants may include them), name?, body_name?

label: Mirror
params: features: [names] | bodies: [names] (combine?: join with the original); plane: XY|XZ|YZ|construction plane name or id|{origin, normal}|{origin, x_dir, y_dir} (origin coordinates may be length expressions; the mirror follows them, or a construction plane)

label: Move/Copy
params: bodies: [names]; translate?: [x,y,z] (length exprs or numbers, applied after rotation); axis?: [x,y,z] (default: world Z with origin, else the body's component's Z, world Z at the root); about?: {edge|face: [x,y,z], body?} (the edge or round face the turn is about, kept as a reference so the turn follows it when an earlier step moves the body; axis gives the turn's sense, and with origin the line used when the edge is not found); angle?: angle expr; origin?: [x,y,z] (length exprs or numbers in world coordinates; default: the body's component's origin, the world origin at the root); matrix?: rigid row-major 3x4 or 4x4, flat or rows (instead of translate/axis/angle/origin); tolerance?: matrix rotation tolerance (default 1e-9, at most 1e-3); copy?: bool (default false; true keeps originals and transforms copies); occurrences?: [occurrence paths, root first] (only with copy: copies each component independently and transforms the copies in world space; reply lists them in occurrences); name?, body_name?, body_names?

label: Offset Face
params: faces: [[x,y,z] points on faces (planar or curved), or face names from model.faces]; distance: expr (positive: outward); body?

label: Circular Pattern
params: features: [names] | bodies: [names] | components: [names]; axis: X|Y|Z | construction axis name (followed when edited) | {origin, dir} (origin coordinates may be length expressions; the pattern follows them) | {edge|face: [x,y,z]} (a straight or circular edge, or a cylinder, cone or torus face: about its axis, followed as the model changes); count; angle? (default 360 deg; partial arcs include both ends); alignment?: left|center|right (default right; original stays fixed); reversed?: bool (Flip; selects the extra side for even centered counts)

label: Pattern on Path
params: features: [names] | bodies: [names]; path_sketch: sketch; path: [curve ids in order]; count; spacing (between instances) | distance (first to last); start?: expr (start point: how far along the path the original sits, the copies measured on from there; default 0, the path's start) | start_fraction?: expr (the start point as 0…1 of the path's length, kept as the path changes); orientation?: identical (copies keep the original's orientation, the default)|path (copies turn with the path, keeping the original's relation to it); flip?: bool (run from the path's other end)

label: Rectangular Pattern
params: features: [names] | bodies: [names] | components: [names]; dir1: [x,y,z]; count1; spacing1; dir2?, count2?, spacing2?; distance1?, distance2?: count_spacing|count_extent|spacing_extent (what sets each direction; default count_spacing; count_extent: count<k> and extent<k>, the distance from the first copy to the last, spacing = extent / (count - 1); spacing_extent: spacing<k> and extent<k>, as many copies as fit, none past the extent's end); extent1?, extent2?: expr (greater than zero); copy_at_end1?, copy_at_end2?: bool (spacing_extent: one more copy exactly at the extent's end when the spacing doesn't divide it, so only the last gap is shorter); alignment?, alignment2?: left|center|right (default right; counts include the original); reversed?, reversed2?: bool (Flip)

label: Pipe
params: path_sketch: sketch; path: [curve ids in order]; diameter: expr; wall?: expr (hollow); operation?, targets?, name?, body_name?

label: Press Pull
params: face: [x,y,z] and distance: expr (positive adds material, negative cuts), or edges: [[x,y,z]…] and distance (a fillet); body?: the body the face or edges are on (for edges, as for solid.fillet); face_body?: the body a flat face is on, used when body is omitted

label: Remove
params: bodies: [names] (removed from here on in the timeline)

label: Replace Face
params: faces: [[x,y,z] points on planar faces, or face names from model.faces]; target: plane (XY|XZ|YZ|construction plane|{origin, normal}) | target_face: [x,y,z] on a parallel planar face; body?

label: Revolve
params: axis: sketch line id | x | y (sketch axes) | X|Y|Z (world) | {type: world, axis: X|Y|Z} (as returned by timeline.inspect) | {sketch, curve} (a line of another sketch, followed in that sketch) | construction axis name (followed when edited) | {origin, dir} (origin: numbers or length expressions, followed when parameters change) | {edge|face: [x,y,z]} (a straight or circular edge, or a cylinder, cone or torus face: about its axis, followed as the model changes); angle?: expr (default 360 deg); angle2?: expr (Two Sides: the other side's angle); direction?: symmetric (angle split either side, independent of axis direction); convention?: sketch_normal|legacy_axis_start (default sketch_normal; legacy retains older angular starts); to?: [x,y,z] (To Object: turn until that face, vertex or point); sketch?, profiles? | face: [x,y,z] (a planar body face as the profile) and face_body?: name (whose face, where faces of several bodies meet) and fixed?: true (the face's plane as a fixed plane, as solid.extrude's), operation?, touching?, targets?, name?, body_name?

label: Rib
params: sketch, curves: [open curve ids, in order]; thickness (across the sketch plane, or across the curves when normal); depth? (default: to the next face); flip?: bool (fill to the other side); direction?: in_plane|normal (grow across the sketch plane, the default, or along its normal); extend?: bool (run the curves' open ends on to the body; default false)

label: Scale
params: bodies: [names]; factor: expr | factors: [x, y, z] exprs; origin?: [x,y,z]

label: Shell
params: faces: [[x,y,z] points on the faces to remove, or face names from model.faces; none: a closed hollow body]; thickness: expr; direction?: inside|outside|both; tangent_chain?: bool (also open faces joined smoothly to the picked ones); body? (needed with no faces when there are several bodies)

label: Sphere
params: radius | diameter: expr; center?: [x,y,z] (numbers in mm or length expressions; default: the origin); operation?, touching?, targets?: [body], name?, body_name?

label: Split Body
params: body: name; plane: XY|XZ|YZ|plane name|{origin, normal} — or tool: {body, point} (a face of a body, its surface extended), tool_plane?: bool (default false; true uses only that face's infinite plane and follows the face) — or sketch: id, line: curve id (a straight sketch line, along the sketch's normal)

label: Split Face
params: faces: [[x,y,z] points on the faces to split, or face names from model.faces]; body?; and the splitting tool: plane: XY|XZ|YZ|plane name|{origin, normal} — or tool: {body, point} (a face of a body, its surface extended) — or sketch: id or name (its curves, along the sketch's normal; each curve on its own, an open one extended past its ends) and loops?: bool (default false: true joins the curves end to end first, so a closed loop cuts along itself only)

label: Sweep
params: sketch: profile sketch; profiles?; face?: [x,y,z] (a planar body face as the profile, its edges projected into a sketch on it) and face_body?: name (whose face, where faces of several bodies meet) and fixed?: true (the face's plane as a fixed plane, as solid.extrude's); path_sketch: sketch; path: [curve ids in order; an entry {sketch, curve} is a curve of that sketch, so the path may join curves of several sketches (#16168)]; path_body?: body name; path_edges?: [points on its edges] (the path is a chain of that body's edges, instead of a sketch's curves); orientation?: perpendicular (default: square to the path, turning with it) | parallel (as drawn: the profile moves without turning; the path must keep crossing its plane) | [x,y,z] (square to the path, its turn about the path fixed by this direction); twist?: angle expr (the profile turns this much about the path over its length; within 4 turns); scale?: expr (the profile's scale at the end, linear along the path; 0.01…100); rails?: [{sketch?: sketch (default path_sketch), curves: [curve ids in order]}] (guide rails, one or two, each meeting every plane square to the path once along it, from the end nearest the path's start: one rail turns the profile so its point where the rail starts stays on the rail and scales it with the rail's distance from the path; two rails carry it between them, its points where they start staying on both; rails take the default orientation, no twist and no scale, and a path without sharp corners); rail_fit?: scale (default: the profile grows and shrinks evenly) | stretch (only across to the rail, between the rails); operation?, touching?, targets?, name?, body_name?

label: Thread
params: face: [x,y,z] on a cylindrical face OR faces: [{body, point:[x,y,z]}, ...] (1 to 1024 selected faces of the same component in one Thread feature; every plural face requires its body identity; exact world body names or unambiguous definition names; do not combine with face); single_face_selection?: bool (default false; true requires exactly one entry in faces and keeps single-face replacement when editing); shared options apply to every face, automatic size fits each independently; cosmetic replies include threads for faces and retain thread as the first; form?: metric|unified|trapezoidal|acme|buttress|buttress_asme|bspp|rp|bspt|npt (default: the one `designation` names, else metric; square is refused: no current standard defines it); designation?: the size, as its standard writes it: metric "M8", "M8x1", "M16xPh3P1.5" (ISO 68-1, ISO 261, ISO 965-1); unified "1/4-20 UNC-2A", "#10-32 UNF" (ASME B1.1, 60 degrees; <size>-<TPI> UNC|UNF|UNEF|UN, optional -1A/-2A/-3A external or -1B/-2B/-3B internal, class retained; size #0..#12 or fractional/decimal inches, major from size, pitch exactly 25.4/TPI; automatic unified uses nearest catalogued UNC, default automatic remains metric); trapezoidal "Tr20x4", "Tr40x14(P7)" (ISO 2904, ISO 2903); buttress "S20x4", "S40x14(P7)" (DIN 513, 3°/30°); acme "1/2-10 ACME" (ASME B1.5); buttress_asme "2.5-8 BUTT" (ASME B1.9, 7°/45°, basic profile; no size table); bspp "G 1/2" (ISO 228-1, 55° parallel); rp "Rp 1/2" (ISO 7-1's parallel internal thread, 55°, an R screws into it; internal only); bspt "R 1/2" external, "Rc 1/2" internal (ISO 7-1, 55°, taper 1 in 16); npt "1/2-14 NPT" (ASME B1.20.1, 60°, taper 1 in 16) — a taper thread starts at a free end (the pipe end or the hole mouth) with its standard diameter there, and an external one runs its standard length unless `length` or `up_to` says otherwise (default: the standard size that fits the face, a shaft its major diameter, a hole its nominal diameter (a 12 mm hole is M12) or else the size whose tap drill it is); hand?: right|left|both (default right; both: a right- and a left-handed groove crossing); old_auto_size?: bool (an automatic size keeps the rule of designs saved before a hole was sized by its nominal diameter: a 12 mm hole is M14; set on those threads, keeps them as they were when edited); steep_flank?: start|end (buttress only, default end: the steep flank of the screw's teeth faces the thread's end, the way its axis points); starts?: 1..8 (lead = starts x pitch: that many grooves, each a turn's starts-th further round; a designation that gives the lead gives the starts); ease_out?: expr|standard|short (modelled threads: the inner end, away from where the thread starts, fades out over this length (shorter than a turn too), its section moving out of the material as it turns; standard 2.5 P, short 1.25 P per ISO 3508; it lies past the full-form length, up to a shoulder's clearance; at a free end, inside the face; without it the groove stops square there, ending in its own profile; the start never fades: it runs off its free end, plain or chamfered (`tip`)); tip?: none|start|both (modelled external threads: start chamfers the end the thread starts from, which must be free, both each free end the thread reaches, ISO 4753's chamfered end, the last teeth tapering into the cone; chamfer_angle?: angle expr to the axis, default 45 deg; chamfer_depth?: expr, radial from the major diameter, default for a metric thread down to the external minor diameter d3 = d - 1.226869 P (ISO 724), the largest ISO 4753 allows; other forms give it); extent?: full|length|up_to (default: length when `length` is given, up_to when `up_to` is, else full: the whole face); length?: expr (from the end the thread starts at); up_to?: [x,y,z] (a point, such as on a shoulder face: the thread runs to its place along the axis) | plane name or {origin, normal} (to where the plane crosses the axis); from?: [x,y,z] near the end of the face the thread starts at (default: the face's only free end, the one with no material past it; else the end the `face` point lies within a third of the face of; a pick in the middle of a face whose ends are alike is refused); modeled?: bool (default false); continuous_flanks?: bool (default true; false keeps the historical half-turn faces and groove-before-chamfer construction). Cosmetic: the model is unchanged, model.threads lists it. Modeled: cuts the thread profile into the body: past a free end the groove runs out a pitch into the air (or through a chamfer); at a shoulder, a head or a blind hole's bottom it stops with its section clear of it, never cutting into it; a hole as wide as the thread or wider is narrowed to the thread's minor diameter first, and the reply's warning says so, unless its wall is open along the thread (a cross hole, a cut through the side, a slanted end), which is refused with the drill to use; a shaft thicker than the thread is refused with the size to make it, never turned down

label: Torus
params: major, minor: expr (radii); center?: [x,y,z] (numbers in mm or length expressions; default: the origin); operation?, touching?, targets?: [body], name?, body_name?

label: Web
params: sketch, curves: [open curve ids] (one wall each); thickness; depth? (default: to the next face); flip?: bool; direction?: in_plane|normal; extend?: bool (default false)

label: Delete Plugin File
params: name → deletes one of the running plugin's files in the design; only from a plugin's own run; one undoable edit

label: Read Plugin Data
params: plugin?: plugin id (required outside a plugin's run; a plugin reads only its own) → name, plugin_version, format (null: none), plugin_format, read_only, document (main JSON or null), blobs: [{name, cache, bytes}]. A plugin reads a document larger than its 1 MiB result, and its files' bytes, through the storage interface (get-document, get-blob), as bytes

label: List Plugin Data
params: → plugins: [{plugin, name, plugin_version, format, installed_version?, status: ready|migrate|missing|disabled|older, read_only, bytes}], the plugins that keep data in the open design; reads plugin manifests, runs no plugin code

label: Patch Plugin Data
params: patch: an RFC 7396 merge patch → applied to the running plugin's main document; only from a plugin's own run; one undoable edit

label: Set Plugin Data
params: document: any JSON, at most 16 MiB → replaces the running plugin's main document in the design, saved in its data_format; only from a plugin's own run; one undoable edit

label: Blend Surface
params: from, to: {body, edges: [[x,y,z]]} (points on the edges of one chain of each body: two picks on the same edge is that one edge, more chain up); continuity?: [g0|g1|g2|g3, g0|g1|g2|g3] (each end, default g1: how much of the surface at the picked edges the blend repeats — the tangent plane, the curvature, or how that curvature changes); bulge?: [number, number] (default 0: how full each end leaves, -0.9 flattest to 3 fullest); align?: [[x,y,z], [x,y,z]] (a point each end leaves towards, when the faces at the picks do not say); seam?: [[x,y,z], [x,y,z]] (a point on each chain its stations start from: two closed chains otherwise pair the way that keeps the blend from twisting; an open chain starts at the end nearer its point; a closed chain blends only to a closed chain); stitch?: bool (sew the blend onto its two bodies where the boundaries meet, replacing them); name?, body_name?

label: Boundary Surface
params: Either a loop of one sketch's curves — sketch?: id|name (default: the sketch being edited); curves: [2 to 4 sketch curve ids in loop order] (each one ends where the next begins and the last where the first does; two: the patch spans between them and leaves each boundary along the tangent across it; three or four: the flat patch of the loop, three collapsing the side opposite the first curve to the corner there); continuity?: g0|g1|g2|g3 | [one per curve] (default g1: how much of the surface across each boundary the patch repeats — a sketch curve's own plane, so g1 and up hold exactly and g0 lets the middle bow); crown?: number -0.9…3 (default 0: how full the middle is, without touching a boundary; two curves only); samples?: 8…512 stations per boundary (default 25) — or a curve network — u: [curve] (two or more one way: the surface lofts through them), v?: [curve] (crossing every u-curve once: two each way give a Coons patch, more a Gordon surface through every curve; a curve that misses another by more than 0.01 mm is refused, naming the pair), each curve "id" (a curve of `sketch`) | {sketch?: id|name, curves: [ids meeting end to end]} (planar or 3D sketch curves) | {body: name, edges: [[x,y,z]] (points on a chain of its edges), continuity?: g0|g1|g2 (default g0; g1 the surface leaves tangent to the face beside a surface's open edges, g2 with its curvature too; on curves of one direction only)} | {point: [x,y,z]} (a side collapsed to a point: a three-sided patch); operation?: new|join (default new; join sews the surface into the body of its first edge curve, a solid when it closes the gap). name?, body_name? (a surface body)

label: Extend
params: body: surface name; edges: [[x,y,z]] (points on boundary edges to push out); distance: expr (unless up_to); mode?: natural (the surface itself continued: a B-spline's end spans continued, which keeps planes and surfaces of revolution on themselves; the default) | tangent (the face continued tangent to its surface across the edge, G1) | curvature (continued keeping the surface's curvature across the edge too, G2); up_to?: plane (XY|XZ|YZ|plane name|{origin, normal}) | {body, point} (a face, its surface extended) | {body} (a whole body, where the surface first runs into any of its faces; natural only) | "bounds" (natural: back to the surface's own bounds, undoing a trim); neighbours?: bool (default true: the edges next to an extended edge are lengthened to meet it; false: the extension's sides run square to the edge); stays_surface?: bool (default true: a result whose shells close stays a surface body, which Stitch makes a solid; false: it becomes a solid, as features saved before it keep)

label: Surface Extrude
params: sketch?: id|name; curves?: [curve ids] (open or closed chains of curves meeting end to end) and/or profiles? (their boundaries; the default when no curves are given); distance: expr (unless `to` or `to_next`); to?: [x,y,z] (To Object: end at the face, vertex or point there; a curved or slanted face trims the walls where they meet its surface); to_offset?: expr (how far past `to`; a flat face square to the extrusion or a point only); to_next?: bool (To Next: each wall runs on, one way as `direction` says, until it first meets a solid or surface body, its faces as they are; a wall that meets none, or runs on past the side of a body covering only part of it, is refused); direction?: positive|negative|symmetric (symmetric: distance is the total, split evenly around the start plane, as solid.extrude); convention?: total_distance|legacy_per_side (as solid.extrude; default total_distance; legacy_per_side: the distance on each side, as older symmetric surface extrudes keep); distance2?: expr; start_offset?: expr; name?, body_name? (a surface body: walls only, no caps)

label: Fair Surface
params: body: surface name; faces?: [[x,y,z]] points on the faces to fair (default: every face); strength?: number (0..1 of the full fairing step, default 1); iterations?: number (1..1000 steps, default 1); keep_edges?: bool (default true: hold the boundary row and the row next to it, so a face keeps meeting its neighbours in position and in tangent); tolerance?: expr mm (how far a control vertex may move, default 0.001 of the body's size). Moves the interior control vertices of each B-spline face to flatten its curvature variation while the boundary stays put: the face keeps its edges and the body its shape within the tolerance, and the warning in the reply carries the energy before and after; name?

disabled_reason: not supported yet (issue #769)
label: Surface Fillet
params: planned: a, b: {body, point} (two faces of separate bodies that meet or cross; the points pick the side the ball rolls on); radius: expr; trim?: both|first|none

label: Surface Loft
params: sections: [{sketch, curves?: [curve ids], profiles?} | {body, edges: [[x,y,z]]}] (2…50 in order; each one chain: a profile without holes, or curves meeting end to end, planar or of a 3D sketch; all open or all closed (all open with a 3D sketch curve); a body edge chain takes the face the chain bounds as the surface the end repeats); continuity?: [g0|g1|g2|g3, g0|g1|g2|g3] (each end, default g0: how much of the surface at the first and last section the loft repeats — the tangent plane, the curvature, or how that curvature changes); crown?: [number, number] (default 0: how full each end leaves, -0.9 flattest to 3 fullest); rails?, rail_fit? (as solid.loft; planar sketch sections only, both ends g0); faced?: bool (default true: through planar sketch sections, the walls face out of the region closed sections bound, as solid.loft's faces do, and an open section's direction crossed with its sketch normal, as surface.extrude's; false: each wall along its skinned surface's normal, as surface lofts saved before it keep); name?, body_name? (a surface body: ruled between two sections, smooth through three or more; no caps); stays_surface?: bool (default true: a result whose shells close stays a surface body, which Stitch makes a solid; false: it becomes a solid, as features saved before it keep)

label: Match Surface
params: body: surface name (the body whose face is rebuilt); faces?: [[x,y,z]] (points on that face, default: the body's first); target: body name (the body the seam must meet); edges: [[x,y,z]] (points on one edge chain of the target: the rebuilt boundary takes its place); order?: g1|g2|g3 (default g2: position and tangent plane, the curvature too, or how that curvature changes along the seam). The far boundary stays where it was and the body keeps its name

label: Midsurface
params: body; max_thickness?: expr (default: the analysis's suggestion); min_thickness?: expr (default 0); min_aspect?: number (default 5: walls whose span is less than this many times their thickness need a decision; lower flags fewer, higher more); pairs?: [[[x,y,z], [x,y,z]]] (a point on each face of each pair to build, as surface.midsurface_analyze lists them; default: the pairs it is sure of); exclude?: [[x,y,z]] (points on faces whose pairs are left out); include_review_pairs?: bool (default false); carry_holes?: bool (default true: holes through both faces stay holes); suppress_holes_below?: expr (default 0: holes no wider are filled); keep_original?: bool (default true); stitch?: bool (default true: one surface body sewn where sheets meet, edges where three meet left open, a solid where the sheets close, as surface.stitch's; false: a body per sheet, and per piece of a sheet a joint cut in pieces across a carried hole); name?, body_name?. The surface halfway between each pair of faces that face each other across material (flat and round walls), joined where walls meet. The feature stores the pairs chosen (a round pair not built yet among them); the reply's warning lists what is not covered

label: Midsurface Analysis
params: body; max_thickness?: expr (default: the suggestion from a first look); min_thickness?: expr (default 0); min_aspect?: number (default 5). Read-only: the proposed pairs (faces, points, thickness, area, coverage, aspect, confidence high|review, notes), the faces in no pair with their reasons (a rim of a wall is accounted for), the wall thicknesses found with a suggested max_thickness each, and what building the confident pairs leaves out

label: Offset Surface
params: faces: [[x,y,z]] (points on the faces); body?; distance: expr (signed, along the faces' normals; 0 copies the faces); chain?: bool (each pick's whole smooth chain of faces); tolerance?: expr (how far a fitted face may stray, default 0.01 mm). Planes and cylinders move exactly; other faces are fitted. A new surface body; stays_surface?: bool (default true: a result whose shells close stays a surface body, which Stitch makes a solid; false: it becomes a solid, as features saved before it keep)

label: Patch
params: sketch?: id|name and profiles? (planar patches of sketch regions) or profiles_3d: [indices] (the sketch's planar 3D-sketch loops, each patched in its own plane, as listed by sketch.inspect) | edges: [[x,y,z]] (points on a closed loop of a body's edges: one face on them, planar when the loop is, else a smooth B-spline surface) and body?; continuity?: g0|g1|g2|g3|g4 (edges only, default g0: how the patch meets the faces beside the loop — g1 their tangent planes, g2 also their curvature across the edges, g3 also its rate of change, g4 the change of that rate) or [{edge: [x,y,z], g: g0|g1|g2|g3|g4}] (those edges so, the rest g0) or {all, edges}; points?: [[x,y,z]] (edges only, up to 64: points the patch passes through); crown?: number −0.9…3 (default 0: only a fitted patch, whose middle becomes fuller by this many times the loop's size — the bump vanishes on the loop, so the face still meets the picked edges and the continuity across them; a loop that is planar and g0 is the exact plane whatever the crown; with points, crown needs a g1 or higher edge); name?, body_name?

label: Reverse Normal
params: body (a surface); faces?: [[x,y,z]] (points on the faces to turn over; default: all of them)

label: Surface Revolve
params: sketch?: id|name; curves?: [curve ids] and/or profiles? (as surface.extrude); axis: sketch line id|x|y|X|Y|Z|{type: world, axis: X|Y|Z}|{sketch, curve} (a line of another sketch, followed in that sketch)|construction axis name|{origin, dir} (origin: numbers or length expressions, followed when parameters change) | {edge|face: [x,y,z]} (a straight or circular edge, or a cylinder, cone or torus face: about its axis, followed as the model changes); angle?: expr (default 360 deg); angle2?: expr (the other side); symmetric?: bool; faced?: bool (default true: each face faces the side Surface Extrude's would, the curve's direction crossed with the sketch normal, so out of a profile; false: each face along its surface's own normal, as surface revolves saved before it keep); stays_surface?: bool (default true: a full turn that closes the walls is a closed surface body, which Stitch makes a solid; false: it becomes a solid, as surface revolves saved before it keep); name?, body_name? (a surface body, no caps)

label: Ruled Surface
params: body; edges: [[x,y,z]] (points on a chain of its edges, open or closed); distance: expr (how far the strip reaches); mode?: normal|tangent|angle|direction (default normal: along the normal of the face beside each edge; tangent: continuing it); angle?: expr (angle mode: from `direction`, else from the face's normal, turned away from the face; 90 deg from the normal is tangent); direction?: [x,y,z] (direction mode: the rulings; angle mode: the reference, e.g. a pull direction for a draft); face?: [x,y,z] (a point on the face the directions come from; default: the face beside the most picked edges); flip?: bool (the other side); corners?: mitre|round (sharp corners of the chain; inside corners are always cut back); far?: [null|[[x,y,z]]] (per chain edge, the interior control points of a free strip's far curve, as the default curve's handles list them; null: the default). A constant ruling, or one keeping its angle to an arc's axis, gives an exact plane, cylinder or cone; where the rulings turn freely along an edge, the strip is the exact ruled surface to a far curve of its own (from corner to corner, fair, near the rulings' ends). A new surface body; stays_surface?: bool (default true: a result whose shells close stays a surface body, which Stitch makes a solid; false: it becomes a solid, as features saved before it keep)

label: Stitch
params: bodies: [names] (surfaces sewn into the first; a solid when they close); tolerance?: expr (default: tight)

label: Surface Sweep
params: sketch?: id|name; curves?: [curve ids] and/or profiles? (as surface.extrude); path_sketch: sketch; path: [curve ids in order] (a path with corners, or 3D curves, gives ruled walls mitred at the corners); path_body?: body name; path_edges?: [points on its edges] (the path is a chain of that body's edges, instead of a sketch's curves); orientation?, twist?, scale?, rails?, rail_fit? (as solid.sweep); name?, body_name? (a surface body, no caps); stays_surface?: bool (default true: a result whose shells close stays a surface body, which Stitch makes a solid; false: it becomes a solid, as features saved before it keep)

label: Thicken
params: bodies: [surface names]; thickness: expr (negative: against the normal); symmetric?: bool; operation?: new|join|cut|intersect; targets?

label: Trim
params: body: surface name; plane: XY|XZ|YZ|plane name|{origin, normal} or tool: {body} (the whole bounded cutting sheet) | {body, point} (a face, its surface extended) or curves: {sketch, curves?: [curve ids] (chains of curves meeting end to end; default every curve), direction?: normal|face_normal|[x,y,z] (swept onto the surface along the sketch's normal, the default, or this direction; face_normal: projected along the surface's own normal, each point of a curve to its nearest point of the surface, and `keep` picks regions)}; keep: [x,y,z] (a point on the side to keep) or [[x,y,z], ...] (points on the regions to keep: the pieces that hang together once cut). Mutual trim: with: another surface (one face each; leave out plane, tool and curves), keep_with: [x,y,z] or [[x,y,z], ...] (what to keep of it); each is cut where the other's surface (extended) meets it; extend?: bool (a surface that stops short of the other is extended to meet it); stitch?: bool (the kept pieces sewn into `body`; `with` is then gone)

params: camera?: Camera (default: current session camera or home view) → camera; turns to that standard view as the axes navigator does, keeping target, distance and projection

label: Visual Style
params: style: shaded_with_edges|shaded|wireframe|shaded_with_hidden_edges → style, index (0..3 in that order)

label: Zoom Mode
params: on?: bool (omitted: toggle) → on?; moving the pointer up over the view zooms in and down zooms out, no button held, until turned off, another mode or Esc

label: Use Window Options as Default
params: window?: pop-out id (default: current or last focused pop-out) → window, options; saves its options as the defaults for new pop-outs
